docs.title: LiftForge
docs.text: LiftForge is a C++ elevator and lift system for Unreal Engine 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8 (Windows 64-bit). It is built for architectural visualisation: cars you can place, resize and operate in minutes, with a Blueprint API that covers everything a car can do.

docs.title: What is in the box
docs.text:
• Nine presets, each with a visual set and a ready-to-place Blueprint: Traction, MRL630, MRL1000, Goods2000, Bed2500, Panoramic, Hydraulic, Platform and Cycle. Passenger, goods, bed, panoramic and hydraulic cars stay within the EN 81-20 maximum car area for their rated load. Sizes are visualisation sizes, inspired by common ISO 4190-1 classes, and catalogue-neutral. The platform and cycle lift sizes are illustrative. See Presets and visual sets.
  • Elevator Builder, an editor tab to create, resize, validate and rebuild cars. See Elevator Builder.
  • Collective control for single cars and bank dispatch with destination calls for groups. See Bank and destination dispatch.
  • Operating modes and faults: Normal, Independent, Maintenance, Fire Recall, Out of Service; door jam, power loss, emergency brake, stuck between floors. See Operating modes and faults.
  • Inspection views: cutaway, exploded view and part labels, for explaining how a lift is built. See Inspection views.
  • A stable Blueprint API: two entry points, a full set of events, status getters and a latent "Move Elevator To Floor" node. See Blueprint API.
  • Desktop demo pawn using Enhanced Input, and an OpenXR VR sample pawn that has not been tested on a real VR headset. See VR setup.
  • Multiplayer (server-authoritative cars for listen and dedicated servers) and NPC riding (AI characters that call, board and ride). See Multiplayer guide and NPC riding guide.
  • Two example maps with all nine presets: LF_Showcase_Warm and LF_Showcase_Noir, in /LiftForge/Examples/Maps/.
  • Source code for all four modules (runtime, AI, demo and editor), with automation tests.

docs.title: A kinematic visualisation, not a controller
docs.text: LiftForge simulates how a lift looks and behaves: motion profiles, doors, calls, modes and faults. It is not a certified control system and not an engineering model of ropes, hydraulics or braking. Check the relevant standard and your local rules for real projects.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Install the plugin.
  2. Follow the Quick start: place a preset and press Play in five minutes.
  3. Read Using your own character if you do not use the demo character.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Generated from the public headers of the Runtime module. Property types are in C++ spelling; the Blueprint display name is in brackets after an enum value.

The tables list the public enums, structs, classes, properties, functions and events of the main Runtime headers, with their Blueprint access and category. Signage (ALFSignage) and the mirror capture (ULFMirrorCaptureComponent) are described in Presets and visual sets, and the AI classes in the NPC riding guide. The Demo and Editor modules (sample pawns, input config, Elevator Builder, asset library) are not part of the frozen API; their Blueprint-visible members also have tooltips. Not frozen: FLFPart, ELFPartRole and the structs of LFNetTypes.h are internal data that can change within 1.x.

docs.title: ELFElevatorType
docs.text:
The purpose of an elevator: a label for your own logic. Only Panoramic changes the build (glazed cabin material). The Drive picks the machinery and the sound.

Member Description Passenger (Passenger) Passenger car for people. Freight (Freight) Goods or service car with a high capacity and a plain cabin. Panoramic (Panoramic) Passenger car with glazed walls. Hydraulic (Hydraulic) Low-rise car lifted by a hydraulic ram. Platform (Platform Lift) Open accessibility platform lift. Cycle (Cycle Lift) Compact car sized for bicycles.

docs.title: ELFDrive
docs.text:
The machine that moves the car. It decides which machinery is generated and which sound plays while moving.

Member Description GearlessTraction (Gearless Traction) Traction machine without a gearbox. GearedTraction (Geared Traction) Traction machine with a gearbox. Hydraulic (Hydraulic) Hydraulic pump and ram.

docs.title: ELFDoorLayout
docs.text:
How the cabin and landing doors open.

Member Description CenterOpening (Center Opening) Two leaves that part at the centre. SideSliding (Side Sliding) One leaf that slides to the side. Telescopic (Telescopic) Several overlapping leaves that slide to the side. Hinged (Hinged) One swing leaf on a hinge.

docs.title: ELFElevatorState
docs.text:
What the car is doing right now. Read it with Get State or listen to On State Changed.

Member Description Idle (Idle) Parked or waiting for a call, doors closed. Opening (Doors Opening) The doors are opening. Open (Doors Open) The doors are fully open and the dwell timer runs. Closing (Doors Closing) The doors are closing. Accelerating (Accelerating) Moving: speeding up after departure. Cruising (Cruising) Moving: at full speed. Decelerating (Decelerating) Moving: slowing down towards the target floor. Leveling (Leveling) Moving: the last centimetres of the approach, creeping to the landing level. Stopped (Stopped) Held after a fault was reset or a trip was interrupted. Needs Resume Operation. Fault (Fault) A fault is active. See Get Fault.

docs.title: ELFElevatorMode
docs.text:
The operating mode of a car. Anything other than Normal discards the queued calls.

Member Description Normal (Normal) Automatic collective control: serves hall and cabin calls. Independent (Independent) Attendant service: serves cabin calls only, hall calls are rejected. Maintenance (Maintenance) Inspection service: no calls, the car moves only with Maintenance Jog. FireRecall (Fire Recall) Fire service phase 1: the car returns to the recall floor and opens its doors there. OutOfService (Out of Service) Out of service: the car stops at the next floor and accepts no calls.

docs.title: ELFFault
docs.text:
A fault that can be injected into a car to test how a project reacts.

Member Description None (None) No fault. DoorJam (Door Jam) The doors are jammed and cannot open or close. PowerLoss (Power Loss) Power loss: the car stops and the cabin lights go out. EmergencyBrake (Emergency Brake) The emergency brake dropped. StuckBetweenFloors (Stuck Between Floors) The car stopped between two floors.

docs.title: ELFDirection
docs.text:
A travel or call direction.

Member Description None (None) No direction: a cabin call, or a car with nothing to do. Up (Up) Towards higher floors. Down (Down) Towards lower floors.

docs.title: ELFElevatorCommand
docs.text:
Everything a button, console, panel or Blueprint can ask an elevator to do. Pass one to Execute Elevator Command, the single entry point that the generated buttons, the operator console and the demo panel all use.

Member Description None (None) No command. Unknown button names resolve to this and are ignored. SelectFloor (Select Floor) Cabin call: send the car to Floor Id. HallCallUp (Hall Call Up) Hall call going up from Floor Id. A linked bank picks the car. HallCallDown (Hall Call Down) Hall call going down from Floor Id. A linked bank picks the car. DestinationCall (Destination Call) Destination call from Origin Floor Id to Floor Id. A linked bank picks the car. OpenDoors (Open Doors) Open the doors at the current landing. CloseDoors (Close Doors) Close the doors. PassengerAlarm (Passenger Alarm) Sound the passenger alarm. EmergencyCall (Emergency Call) Emergency call button of the car operating panel. Raises On Command Executed only. Help (Help) Help button of the car operating panel. Raises On Command Executed only. Phone (Phone) Phone button of the car operating panel. Raises On Command Executed only. ToggleCutaway (Toggle Cutaway) Show or hide the cutaway of the shaft wall. ToggleExploded (Toggle Exploded View) Switch the exploded inspection view on or off. Switching it on puts the car into Maintenance. ToggleLabels (Toggle Part Labels) Show or hide the inspection labels of the parts. ToggleOverload (Toggle Simulated Overload) Simulate an overloaded cabin, or clear the simulated load. ToggleObstruction (Toggle Simulated Obstruction) Simulate a blocked door light curtain, or clear it. ModeNormal (Mode: Normal) Set the mode to Normal. ModeIndependent (Mode: Independent) Set the mode to Independent. ModeMaintenance (Mode: Maintenance) Set the mode to Maintenance. ModeFireRecall (Mode: Fire Recall) Set the mode to Fire Recall. ModeOutOfService (Mode: Out Of Service) Set the mode to Out Of Service. FaultDoorJam (Fault: Door Jam) Inject a door jam fault. FaultPowerLoss (Fault: Power Loss) Inject a power loss fault. FaultEmergencyBrake (Fault: Emergency Brake) Inject an emergency brake fault. FaultStuckBetweenFloors (Fault: Stuck Between Floors) Inject a stuck-between-floors fault. ResetFault (Reset Fault) Clear the active fault and hold the car until Resume. Resume (Resume) Release the hold after a reset and recover to the nearest floor. JogUp (Maintenance Jog Up) Maintenance jog to the next floor above. JogDown (Maintenance Jog Down) Maintenance jog to the next floor below.

docs.title: ELFCallRejectReason
docs.text:
Why a call was not accepted. Reported by On Call Rejected and by Move Elevator To Floor.

Member Description None (None) The call was accepted. UnknownFloor (Unknown Floor) The floor is not served by the car. SameFloor (Same Floor) The origin and the destination of the call are the same floor. InvalidDirection (Invalid Direction) A hall call needs Up or Down, and not Up at the top floor or Down at the bottom floor. AccessDenied (Access Denied) The access level of the caller is below the access level of the floor. Fault (Fault Active) A fault is active. ResumeRequired (Resume Required) A fault was reset and the car waits for Resume Operation. OutOfService (Out Of Service) The car is out of service. Maintenance (Maintenance Mode) The car is in Maintenance mode. FireRecall (Fire Recall Mode) The car is in Fire Recall mode. IndependentService (Independent Service) The car is in Independent mode, which accepts cabin calls only. InvalidConfiguration (Invalid Configuration) The configuration of the car is invalid, so it does not operate. NoElevatorAvailable (No Elevator Available) A bank found no car that can serve the call.

docs.title: FLFFloor
docs.text:
One landing served by an elevator.

Member Description FName Id read/write, Elevator Unique name used by every call and getter to refer to this floor, for example G, L1 or B2. FString Label read/write, Elevator Text shown on the displays and buttons. Not translated. double Elevation = 0 read/write, Elevator Landing height above the actor origin. Floors must be listed from the lowest to the highest. bool bFrontEntrance = true read/write, Elevator The landing has an entrance on the front side of the car. bool bRearEntrance = false read/write, Elevator The landing has an entrance on the rear side of the car (a through car). int32 AccessLevel = 0 read/write, Elevator Minimum access level a caller needs to travel to or from this floor. 0 is open to everyone. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Announcement read/write, Elevator Spoken announcement played on arrival. Optional.

docs.title: FLFAudioPack
docs.text:
The sounds of an elevator. Any sound may be left empty.

Member Description float Volume = 0.35f read/write, Elevator|Audio Master volume of every sound of the car. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Motor read/write, Elevator Traction machine loop, played while the car moves. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> HydraulicPump read/write, Elevator Hydraulic pump loop, played instead of Motor by hydraulic drives. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> DoorMotor read/write, Elevator Door motor loop, played while the doors move. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Brake read/write, Elevator Brake sound, played at departure and arrival. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Latch read/write, Elevator Door latch sound, played when the doors reach closed. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Button read/write, Elevator Button press sound. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Chime read/write, Elevator Arrival chime. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Alarm read/write, Elevator Passenger alarm and fault alarm. Plays once; a looping sound stops only when a fault is reset. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> Overload read/write, Elevator Overload warning, played when the load rises above the capacity. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> DoorsOpening read/write, Elevator Spoken announcement when the doors open. Optional. TSoftObjectPtr<USoundBase> DoorsClosing read/write, Elevator Spoken announcement when the doors close. Optional.

docs.title: FLFPartMesh
docs.text:
A mesh of a visual set and the nominal size it was authored at.

Member Description TSoftObjectPtr<UStaticMesh> Mesh read/write, Elevator|Art The static mesh placed for the part role. FVector SourceDimensions = FVector(100) read/write, Elevator|Art Size of the mesh as authored. The part is scaled from this to the size the configuration needs. bool bPreserveMaterialSlots = true read/write, Elevator|Art Keep the material slots of the mesh instead of applying the configuration materials. TArray<TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface>> MaterialOverrides read/write, Elevator|Art Materials that replace the slots of the mesh, in slot order.

docs.title: ULFVisualSet
docs.text:
A set of authored meshes, one per part role. Cars that reference a visual set use it instead of the generated kit.

Member Description FString Description read/write, Elevator|Art A short description of the look of the set. TMap<FName, FLFPartMesh> PartMeshes read/write, Elevator|Art The mesh of each part role, keyed by role name (for example CabinWall or DoorFrame).

docs.title: ELFImportedPartRole
docs.text:
What a part of an imported assembly is and how it moves.

Member Description CabinFloor (Cabin Floor) The floor of the cabin, which pawns stand on. An assembly has exactly one. CabinRigid (Cabin Rigid) Any other part that rides with the cabin. CabinDoor (Cabin Door) A leaf of the cabin door. LandingFixed (Landing Fixed) A part that stays at its landing. LandingDoor (Landing Door) A leaf of a landing door. ShaftFixed (Shaft Fixed) A part fixed in the shaft, placed relative to the actor.

docs.title: FLFImportedPart
docs.text:
One mesh of an imported source assembly, placed instead of the generated kit geometry.

Member Description FName Name read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly Unique name of the part within the assembly. ELFImportedPartRole Role = ELFImportedPartRole::CabinRigid read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly What the part is and how it moves. TSoftObjectPtr<UStaticMesh> Mesh read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly The static mesh of the part. FTransform RelativeTransform = FTransform::Identity read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly Transform relative to the cabin datum (cabin roles), the landing floor (landing roles) or the actor (shaft). FName FloorId read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly Floor the part belongs to. Needed for landing roles. int32 Leaf = 0 read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly Door leaf, 0 or 1. Door roles only. bool bRear = false read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly The part belongs to the rear entrance. bool bCollision = true read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly The part blocks pawns. The cabin floor and doors need collision. TArray<TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface>> MaterialOverrides read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly Materials that replace the slots of the mesh, in slot order.

docs.title: ELFCabinScreen
docs.text:
Where a visual set's cabin advertising screen is placed, if the set has one (roles CabinScreenCorner / CabinScreenWall).

Member Description None (None) No screen in the car. Corner (Ceiling Corner) A ceiling-corner screen in the front-left corner, facing the passengers. Wall (Side Wall) A portrait panel on the side wall next to the car operating panel.

docs.title: FLFElevatorConfiguration
docs.text:
Everything that describes one elevator: its floors, size, speed, doors, capacity, look and sounds.

Member Description FString DisplayName = TEXT("Passenger elevator") read/write, Elevator Name of the elevator, shown on the operator console and panel. ELFElevatorType Type = ELFElevatorType::Passenger read/write, Elevator Purpose of the elevator. ELFDrive Drive = ELFDrive::GearlessTraction read/write, Elevator The machine that moves the car. ELFDoorLayout DoorLayout = ELFDoorLayout::CenterOpening read/write, Elevator How the doors open. TArray<FLFFloor> Floors read/write, Elevator The landings, listed from the lowest to the highest. FName InitialFloor = TEXT("G") read/write, Elevator Floor the car starts at. FName RecallFloor = TEXT("G") read/write, Elevator Floor the car returns to in Fire Recall mode. float CabinWidth = 220 read/write, Elevator Inside width of the cabin. float CabinDepth = 240 read/write, Elevator Inside depth of the cabin. float CabinHeight = 270 read/write, Elevator Inside height of the cabin. float DoorWidth = 130 read/write, Elevator Clear width of the door opening. float DoorHeight = 225 read/write, Elevator Clear height of the door opening. float MaxSpeed = 160 read/write, Elevator Rated speed of the car. float MaxAcceleration = 80 read/write, Elevator Largest acceleration and deceleration of the car. float MaxJerk = 120 read/write, Elevator Largest rate of change of acceleration in cm/s^3 (the engine has no unit for it), which sets how smooth starts and stops feel. float DoorSeconds = 1.5 read/write, Elevator Time the doors take to open or close. float DwellSeconds = 4 read/write, Elevator Time the doors stay open before they close on their own. float CapacityKg = 1000 read/write, Elevator Rated load. The car is overloaded above this and does not travel. float PassengerMassKg = 75 read/write, Elevator Mass counted for each pawn in the cabin. float StarvationSeconds = 30 read/write, Elevator|Dispatch Bounded waiting: a call older than this is served on the next trip, even if collective control would pass it by to serve calls in the current travel direction first. float DirectionChangePenaltySeconds = 10 read/write, Elevator|Dispatch Seconds the arrival estimate adds when a moving car must reverse to serve a hall call (bank dispatch cost). float DetailDrawDistance = 8000 read/write, Elevator|Detail Distance from the camera beyond which the small cabin and shaft details are hidden. TSoftObjectPtr<ULFVisualSet> VisualSet read/write, Elevator|Art Authored look. Empty builds the elevator from the generated kit. TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> CabinMaterial read/write, Elevator Cabin wall material of the generated kit. Empty uses the project default. TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> DoorMaterial read/write, Elevator Door material of the generated kit. Empty uses the project default. TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> FloorMaterial read/write, Elevator Cabin floor material of the generated kit. Empty uses the project default. TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> MachineryMaterial read/write, Elevator Machinery material of the generated kit. Empty uses the project default. TSoftObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface> ShaftMaterial read/write, Elevator Hoistway wall material. Empty uses the project default; a glass material makes a glazed shaft (panoramic lift on an atrium face). bool bMirrorCapture = false read/write, Elevator|Art A real reflection on the rear wall's mirror panel (slot M_HQ_Mirror): a scene capture from the viewer's reflected position, sampled per world point by the mirror material. Software Lumen shows the stainless doors black in a mirror; this renders the mirror view for real while a viewer stands in front of it. Needs the project setting "Support global clip plane for Planar Reflections". Off by default; the mirrored presets of the showcase turn it on. ELFCabinScreen CabinScreen = ELFCabinScreen::None read/write, Elevator|Art Cabin advertising screen placed from the visual set (roles CabinScreenCorner / CabinScreenWall). None places no screen. TSoftObjectPtr<UTexture> CabinScreenImage read/write, Elevator|Art Picture shown on the cabin screen (any texture, for example a T_LF_Screen_* sample). Empty keeps the screen material's own image. float LandingWallOffset = 0 read/write, Elevator Distance from the landing door plane to the finished face of the landing wall in front of it. The hall station, hall lanterns, landing indicators and displays are mounted on that face. 0 (the 1.0 layout) mounts them on the door plane itself; a wall 6 cm in front of the doors hides the open leaves and gives the door frame a 4 cm reveal. float CabinLightTemperature = 4000 read/write, Elevator|Lighting Colour temperature of the cabin point light and the two ceiling fill lights. 4000 K (the default) is the 1.0 look. bool bCabinLightShadows = false read/write, Elevator|Lighting Lets the cabin lights cast shadows. Off by default: three shadow-casting lights per car cost frame time. FString Provenance = TEXT("Original authored visualization; dimensions are configurable assumptions.") read/write, Elevator Free text that records where the data of this configuration comes from. FString BrandText read/write, Elevator|Display Optional brand line printed on the cabin panel. Empty (the default) prints nothing. FLFAudioPack Audio read/write, Elevator Sounds of the elevator.

docs.title: ULFElevatorPreset
docs.text:
A data asset that stores one elevator configuration, so many cars can share it.

Member Description FLFElevatorConfiguration Configuration read/write, Elevator The configuration that cars using this preset operate with.

docs.title: FLFRequest
docs.text:
A registered call: a hall call (Direction Up or Down) or a cabin call (bCabin, Direction None).

Member Description FName FloorId read only, Elevator Floor the call goes to (cabin call) or is made from (hall call). ELFDirection Direction = ELFDirection::None read only, Elevator Direction of a hall call. None for a cabin call. bool bCabin = false read only, Elevator True for a cabin call made from inside the car. double AcceptedAt = 0 read only, Elevator Simulation time at which the call was accepted.

docs.title: ULFLoadComponent
docs.text:
Add to an actor to give it a mass in the cabin. Without it a pawn weighs the car's passenger mass.

Member Description float LoadKg = 75 read/write, Elevator Mass this actor adds to the car load while it stands in the cabin.

docs.title: ULFButtonComponent
docs.text:
A pressable button. Press it with Press Button, or let a pawn point at it and use Trace Button to find it. The button runs its Command through its Elevator (or Bank), the same path Blueprints use.

Member Description TObjectPtr<ALFElevator> Elevator read/write, Elevator The elevator the button controls. TObjectPtr<ALFElevatorBank> Bank read/write, Elevator Bank that dispatches hall and destination calls of this button. Empty uses the bank of the elevator. FName FloorId read/write, Elevator Floor the button selects, calls from or goes to. FName OriginFloorId read/write, Elevator Floor a destination call starts from. FName Command = TEXT("Select") read/write, Elevator Button name of the command: Select, Up, Down, Destination, Open, Close, Alarm and so on. Use Set Command Type to pick a command from the enum instead of typing a name; an unknown name does nothing. FString Caption read/write, Elevator Text drawn on the button. ELFElevatorCommand GetCommandType() const pure, Elevator|Interaction The command of this button as an enum. None when Command holds an unknown name. void SetCommandType(ELFElevatorCommand NewCommand) callable, Elevator|Interaction Sets Command from the enum, so a typo in a button name is not possible. bool PressButton(int32 AccessLevel = 0) callable, Elevator|Interaction Presses the button: runs its command through Execute Elevator Command and plays the press animation and sound. Returns true when a call was accepted or a service command ran. static ULFButtonComponent* TraceButton(const UObject* WorldContextObject, const FVector& Start, const FVector& Direction, AActor* Ignore = nullptr, double Distance = 450) callable, Elevator|Interaction Finds the button in front of a pawn: a visibility trace from Start along Direction that returns the button it hits, or null. The desktop, VR and HUD pickers of the demo use it.

docs.title: ELFPartRole
docs.text: How a generated or imported part animates. Parts that never move after a build are Fixed.

docs.title: FLFPart
docs.text: One generated or imported mesh of an assembly and the data AnimateParts needs to move it.

docs.title: ALFElevator
docs.text:
One elevator: a car, its doors, buttons, displays, machinery and shaft, built from a preset or a configuration and operated by collective control. Every way to operate it goes through two entry points: Execute Elevator Command (doors, floors, modes, faults, inspection views) and Call To Floor (a trip between two floors). The generated buttons, the operator console, the demo panel and your own Blueprints all use them. Multiplayer: the server runs the car and replicates a compact state; clients rebuild the motion, doors, displays, sounds and events from it. On a client every command function is sent to the server through the local player's ULFElevatorInteractorComponent, and returns true when it was sent.

Member Description TObjectPtr<ULFElevatorPreset> Preset read/write, Elevator|Configuration Data asset that holds the configuration of this car. Used unless Use Configuration Override is on. Replicated: a change on the server rebuilds the car on every client. FLFElevatorConfiguration Configuration read/write, Elevator|Configuration The configuration of this car, used when there is no preset or when Use Configuration Override is on. Replicated. bool bUseConfigurationOverride = false read/write, Elevator|Configuration Use Configuration instead of the preset, so one car can differ from its preset. Replicated. TArray<FLFImportedPart> ImportedParts read/write, Elevator|Imported Assembly When non-empty, RebuildAssembly places these source meshes instead of the generated kit geometry. ValidateConfiguration checks them alongside the configuration. Call MarkConfigurationDirty() or RebuildAssembly() after changing this from gameplay code. Replicated. FName ElevatorId = TEXT("A") read/write, Elevator|Identity Short name of the car within its bank, for example A or B. Also used to break ties between cars. Replicated. TObjectPtr<ALFElevatorBank> DispatchBank read/write, Elevator|Identity Bank that dispatches this car's hall calls. The bank lists the car as a member automatically. With World Partition prefer BankName (no hard actor reference). Replicated. FName BankName read/write, Elevator|Identity Name of the bank this car belongs to. Cars and banks with the same BankName find each other at runtime through the world's LiftForge registry, so they can live in different World Partition cells. Empty: only DispatchBank and the bank's Elevators list link them. Replicated. bool bCutaway = true read/write, Elevator|Inspection Hide the shaft wall on the side of the viewer so the car can be seen travelling. bool bShowPartLabels = false read/write, Elevator|Inspection Show a text label on every part. float ExplodedAmount = 0 read/write, Elevator|Inspection How far the parts are moved apart for the exploded inspection view: 0 assembled, 1 fully exploded. bool bShaftCollision = true read/write, Elevator|Collision Invisible blocking walls around the hoistway, open only at the landing entrances, so players cannot walk into the shaft or fall into the pit. They block pawns and physics bodies only. Replicated. bool bStaticFixedParts = false read/write, Elevator|Performance Build the parts that never move (shaft, rails, frames, sills, machine room) with Static mobility. Cheaper to render, but the actor's root becomes Static, so the elevator cannot be moved at runtime, and projects with static lighting report these parts as unbuilt until lighting is built. The exploded view switches them to Movable when it is used. Replicated. float SimulatedLoadKg = 0 read/write, Elevator|Load Extra load added to what stands in the cabin, to test the overload behaviour without a pawn. bool bSimulatedObstruction = false read/write, Elevator|Sensors Treat the door light curtain as blocked, to test the door reversal without a pawn. TObjectPtr<USceneComponent> CabinRoot read only, Elevator|Components Root of everything that rides with the car. TObjectPtr<UBoxComponent> CabinSensor read only, Elevator|Components Volume that weighs what stands in the cabin. TObjectPtr<UBoxComponent> DoorSensor read only, Elevator|Components Light curtain of the front door. TObjectPtr<UBoxComponent> RearDoorSensor read only, Elevator|Components Light curtain of the rear door. FLFFloorEvent OnArrival event, Elevator|Events The car stopped level at a floor. Raised before the doors start to open. FLFFloorEvent OnDeparture event, Elevator|Events The car left a floor. FLFStateEvent OnStateChanged event, Elevator|Events The state of the car changed. FLFModeEvent OnModeChanged event, Elevator|Events The operating mode changed. FLFFaultEvent OnFaultChanged event, Elevator|Events A fault started or was reset. FLFDoorEvent OnDoorsChanged event, Elevator|Events The doors reached fully open (Open true) or fully closed (Open false). FLFFloorEvent OnDoorsOpening event, Elevator|Events|Doors The doors started to open at a floor. FLFFloorEvent OnDoorsOpened event, Elevator|Events|Doors The doors are fully open at a floor. Passengers can board. FLFFloorEvent OnDoorsClosing event, Elevator|Events|Doors The doors started to close. FLFFloorEvent OnDoorsClosed event, Elevator|Events|Doors The doors are fully closed. FLFCallRejectedEvent OnCallRejected event, Elevator|Events A call was refused. The reason says why. A bank raises its own event when it finds no car. FLFOverloadEvent OnOverloadChanged event, Elevator|Events The load rose above the capacity (true) or fell back below it (false). FLFObstructionEvent OnObstructionChanged event, Elevator|Events The door light curtain became blocked (true) or free (false). FLFPassengerEvent OnPassengerEntered event, Elevator|Events An actor that adds load (a pawn, an actor with a load component or a physics body) entered the cabin. FLFPassengerEvent OnPassengerExited event, Elevator|Events An actor left the cabin. Not raised for an actor that was destroyed inside the cabin. FLFCommandEvent OnCommandExecuted event, Elevator|Events A command ran through Execute Elevator Command. Also the way to react to the Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons. bool ExecuteElevatorCommand(ELFElevatorCommand Command, FName FloorId = NAME_None, int32 AccessLevel = 0, FName OriginFloorId = NAME_None, ALFElevatorBank* BankOverride = nullptr) callable, Elevator|Commands Runs one command. This is the single entry point for the generated buttons, the operator console, the demo panel and Blueprints. Floor Id is the floor of a call; Origin Floor Id is the floor a destination call starts from. Hall and destination calls go through the bank of the car (or Bank Override) when there is one. docs.title: ALFElevatorBank
docs.text:
Dispatches hall and destination calls to a group of cars. A car belongs to a bank when the bank lists it, when the car names the bank in Dispatch Bank, when its Bank Name matches, or after Register Elevator. Membership is two-way: a car that names a bank is listed by it, and a bank that lists a car becomes the car's Dispatch Bank, so hall buttons always reach the bank. Multiplayer: the bank dispatches on the server only. On a client, Request Hall Call and Request Destination send the call to the server (through the local player's interactor) and return null; the requesting client then hears On Assigned or On Call Rejected for its own call.

FName BankName read/write, Elevator Bank Cars whose BankName matches also belong to this bank. They are found at runtime through the world's LiftForge registry as they stream in, so bank and cars can live in different cells. float DestinationGroupingBonusSeconds = 15 read/write, Elevator Bank Seconds taken off a car's estimate when it already carries a call with the same origin and destination. FLFAssignmentEvent OnAssigned event, Elevator Bank|Events A call was assigned to a car. FLFBankRejectedEvent OnCallRejected event, Elevator Bank|Events A call could not be placed. The reason says why (no car, access, unknown floor, or the reason the chosen car gave). ALFElevator* RequestHallCall(FName OriginFloorId, ELFDirection Direction, int32 AccessLevel = 0) callable, Elevator Bank Hall call: a passenger at Origin Floor Id wants to go in a direction. The bank picks the car with the shortest estimate and returns it, or returns null and raises On Call Rejected. ALFElevator* RequestDestination(FName OriginFloorId, FName DestinationFloorId, int32 AccessLevel = 0) callable, Elevator Bank Destination call: a passenger at Origin Floor Id wants to go to Destination Floor Id. The bank picks the car, calls it to the origin and selects the destination when its doors open there. Returns the car, or null and raises On Call Rejected. bool RegisterElevator(ALFElevator* Elevator) callable, Elevator Bank Adds a car to the bank and makes the bank the car's Dispatch Bank. Returns false when the car belongs to another bank. bool UnregisterElevator(ALFElevator* Elevator) callable, Elevator Bank Removes a car from the bank and clears its Dispatch Bank. Returns false when the car was not a member. bool ValidateBank(TArray<FString>& Errors) const callable, Elevator Bank Checks the bank: it has cars, no car belongs to another bank, no two cars share an id, and every car shares a floor with another car. docs.title: ULFElevatorRegistry
docs.text:
Tracks the elevators and banks that have begun play in a world. Cars and banks register in BeginPlay and unregister in EndPlay, so with World Partition they appear and disappear as their cells stream. Cars and banks that share a BankName find each other here without hard actor references, which would otherwise force them into the same cell. In multiplayer it also keeps the clock that clients run the replicated cars on, and on the server gives every player an interactor (see ULFElevatorInteractorComponent).

docs.title: ULFElevatorInteractorComponent
docs.text:
Sends a player's elevator requests (buttons, the operator console, UI commands, destination input) to the server in multiplayer. The server checks every request and uses its own Access Level for it; the client never decides that. You rarely call it yourself: on a client, Execute Elevator Command, Call To Floor, the command functions of ALFElevator, the bank's Request Hall Call and Request Destination and Press Button all route through the local player's interactor. LiftForge adds one to every player controller on the server (Project Settings > LiftForge > Multiplayer), or add it to your PlayerController or pawn. Call its functions directly for split-screen, where several local players share one machine.

Member Description int32 AccessLevel = 0 read/write, Elevator|Network Highest access level the server grants this player. Set it on the server (for example in the game mode's Post Login); a request uses the lower of this and the level the caller asked for. Replicated to the owning client for display. bool bAllowServiceCommands = false read/write, Elevator|Network Lets this player run service commands: modes, faults, reset, resume, jog, inspection views and the simulated load and obstruction. Off (the default): only calls, doors, alarm and the help buttons. Checked on the server. Turn it on only for players who may stop or fault a car. float MaxRequestDistance = 0 read/write, Elevator|Network The server refuses requests for a car (or bank) farther than this from the player's pawn. 0 turns the check off. The distance is measured to the bounds of the car and its shaft. int32 MaxRequestsPerSecond = 20 read/write, Elevator|Network Requests per second the server accepts from this player; extra ones are dropped with a warning. LiftForge calls this for every player when elevators are in a networked world; call it yourself to set Access Level early.

docs.title: Blueprint API
docs.text:
This page explains how the API fits together. The API reference lists the runtime and interaction classes. The AI classes are described in the NPC riding guide, and signage in Presets and visual sets.

The 1.0 API is stable: names, parameter order and enum values do not change within 1.x; new members are added with defaults. Every item is a Blueprint node, event or property with a tooltip unless it is marked C++ only. A function's Blueprint name is its C++ name split into words (SelectFloor is Select Floor).

docs.title: 1. The two entry points
docs.text:
Everything that operates a car goes through two functions on ALFElevator. The generated buttons (ULFButtonComponent::PressButton), the operator console, the demo control panel and Blueprints all call them, and so does any network or AI layer you add. A network or AI layer therefore only has to sit in front of these two.

Entry point Use ExecuteElevatorCommand(Command, FloorId, AccessLevel, OriginFloorId, BankOverride) Any ELFElevatorCommand: cabin call, hall call, destination call, doors, modes, faults, reset, resume, jog, inspection toggles. Returns true when a call was accepted or a service command ran. Raises OnCommandExecuted. CallToFloor(FloorId, OriginFloorId, AccessLevel) A trip for a passenger waiting at OriginFloorId who wants to go to FloorId on this car. The car is called to the origin and, when its doors are open there, the destination is selected. An empty origin is a cabin call.

Routing rules of ExecuteElevatorCommand:

  • SelectFloor queues a cabin call on the car.
  • HallCallUp / HallCallDown go to the bank of the car (BankOverride, else GetDispatchBank()), which picks the car; with no bank the car queues the call itself.
  • DestinationCall goes to Bank->RequestDestination(OriginFloorId, FloorId); with no bank it is CallToFloor(FloorId, OriginFloorId) on this car.
  • EmergencyCall, Help and Phone have no built-in behaviour. They are accepted and raise OnCommandExecuted, which is how a project reacts to those buttons.
  • A bank-only panel (a button with a Bank and no Elevator) calls ALFElevatorBank::RequestHallCall / RequestDestination, the bank's own entry points.

ELFElevatorCommand and the shared table:

  • ULFButtonComponent::Command is still an FName, because levels saved before the enum existed store it. The names never change (Select, Up, Down, Destination, Open, Close, Alarm, EmergencyCall, Help, Phone, Cutaway, Exploded, Labels, Overload, Obstruction, Normal, Independent, Maintenance, FireRecall, OutOfService, DoorJam, PowerLoss, EmergencyBrake, Stuck, Reset, Resume, JogUp, JogDown).
  • GetCommandType / SetCommandType convert between the name and the enum. A button whose name is not in the table logs one warning when pressed and does nothing, instead of failing silently.
  • C++ only (LFCommands.h, namespace LiftForge::Commands): Info(Command) returns FLFCommandInfo (button name, console caption, panel label, bIsCall); FromButtonName, ToButtonName, ServiceCommands() (the 21 service commands in console and panel order) and FloorCaption. The console and the panel both build from it. The old per-file tables and LFNames.h::Command are gone.

docs.title: 2. Events and their order
docs.text:
All events are multicast delegates on ALFElevator (the bank has OnAssigned and OnCallRejected). They fire on the game thread, from inside the call or tick that causes them.

Event Parameters Fires OnDeparture Elevator, FloorId The car leaves a floor (FloorId is the floor it leaves). OnArrival Elevator, FloorId The car stops level at a floor, before the doors start to open. Also fires at a stop where the doors stay shut (fire recall stopover; the stop after Maintenance was entered while moving). OnStateChanged Elevator, State Every change of ELFElevatorState. OnDoorsOpening Elevator, FloorId The state becomes Opening. OnDoorsOpened Elevator, FloorId The state becomes Open (doors fully open). OnDoorsClosing Elevator, FloorId The state becomes Closing. OnDoorsClosed Elevator, FloorId The doors reach fully closed. OnDoorsChanged Elevator, bOpen Fully open (true) or fully closed (false). Kept from 0.x. OnModeChanged Elevator, Mode The operating mode changes. OnFaultChanged Elevator, Fault A fault starts or is reset (Fault None). OnCallRejected Elevator, FloorId, Reason A call is refused. Reasons: ELFCallRejectReason. OnOverloadChanged Elevator, bOverloaded The load crosses the capacity, either way. OnObstructionChanged Elevator, bObstructed The door light curtain (or the simulated flag) becomes blocked or free. OnPassengerEntered / OnPassengerExited Elevator, Passenger An actor that adds load (pawn, actor with ULFLoadComponent, simulating physics body) enters or leaves the cabin volume. An actor destroyed inside the cabin leaves without an exit event. OnCommandExecuted Elevator, Command, FloorId, bAccepted After ExecuteElevatorCommand ran (also for refused commands).

Order guarantees, tested by LiftForge.API.EventOrder. Over one trip with the dwell time running out:

OnDeparture, OnStateChanged(Accelerating ... Leveling), OnStateChanged(Idle), OnArrival, OnStateChanged(Opening), OnDoorsOpening, OnStateChanged(Open), OnDoorsOpened, OnDoorsChanged(true), OnStateChanged(Closing), OnDoorsClosing, OnStateChanged(Idle), OnDoorsChanged(false), OnDoorsClosed.

So a door event always follows the matching state change, and when a handler runs the getters already show the new state. Change from 0.x: OnDoorsChanged(false) used to fire before the state became Idle; it now fires after, like the open case.

An obstruction while the doors close gives OnObstructionChanged(true), OnStateChanged(Opening), OnDoorsOpening, ..., OnDoorsOpened (the doors reverse). A mode change raises OnModeChanged first, before any state change it causes.

The light curtain is read while the doors are not fully closed, or whenever something is bound to OnObstructionChanged, so a parked car with closed doors and no listener does not query the overlaps.

docs.title: Call rejection reasons
docs.text: ELFCallRejectReason: UnknownFloor, SameFloor, InvalidDirection (no direction, Up at the top, Down at the bottom), AccessDenied, Fault, ResumeRequired (reset, waiting for Resume), OutOfService, Maintenance, FireRecall, IndependentService (hall call in Independent mode), InvalidConfiguration, NoElevatorAvailable (bank only). GetLastCallRejection returns the reason of the last call (None after an accepted call). A bank forwards the reason of the car it chose, or reports UnknownFloor / AccessDenied / NoElevatorAvailable / SameFloor itself through its own OnCallRejected(OriginFloorId, DestinationFloorId, Reason).

docs.text: IsMoving, GetTargetFloor (the floor of the trip in progress; None when not moving), GetTravelDirection (the committed direction, None when the car has nothing to do; it stays set while the doors are open), GetFloors, GetFloorIndex (-1 for an unknown floor), GetCurrentFloor, GetState, GetOperatingMode, GetFault, GetDoorFraction, GetCarElevation, GetCarVelocity, GetRequests, IsOverloaded, IsDoorObstructed, GetLoadKg, GetOccupants, CanServeFloor, EstimateArrivalSeconds, GetStatusText, GetLastCallRejection, GetDispatchBank, GetCabinFloor. GetConfigurationRef() is the C++ only const-reference accessor of the configuration.

docs.title: 4. Move Elevator To Floor (latent Blueprint node)
docs.text:
ULFMoveElevatorToFloorAction::MoveElevatorToFloor(WorldContext, Elevator, FloorId, OriginFloorId, AccessLevel, TimeoutSeconds), shown as Move Elevator To Floor with two exec outputs:

  • Arrived (Elevator, FloorId): the car is level with FloorId and its doors are fully open. With OriginFloorId the node counts only after the car has opened its doors at the origin.
  • Failed (Elevator, ELFMoveFailure, ELFCallRejectReason): CallRejected (reason set), Fault, ModeChanged (any mode other than Normal discards the queued calls), ElevatorDestroyed, TimedOut (TimeoutSeconds > 0), Cancelled (Cancel).

Exactly one of the two fires, once. It completes at once if the car already stands open at the floor. In C++ call Activate() after creating it (Blueprints do this automatically).

docs.title: 5. Banks, registration and validation
docs.text:
• A car belongs to a bank when the bank lists it in Elevators, when the car names the bank in DispatchBank, when BankName matches, or after ALFElevatorBank::RegisterElevator.
  • Linking is two-way and automatic. At BeginPlay a car that names a bank calls RegisterElevator on it, and a bank calls it for every car it lists, so the car's DispatchBank is set and its hall buttons reach the bank. The authored Elevators array is never edited: registered cars are kept in a transient list and GetMembers returns the union.
  • RegisterElevator returns false (and logs) when the car already belongs to another bank or its BankName differs. UnregisterElevator removes the car and clears its DispatchBank. A call assigned to a car that leaves the bank is reassigned on the next bank tick.
  • ValidateBank(Errors): no cars, a car that belongs to another bank, a BankName conflict, two cars with the same ElevatorId, a car that shares no floor with the others. In the editor CheckForErrors reports the same in Map Check; at BeginPlay the bank logs one warning.
  • Calls assigned by the bank are re-evaluated on every bank tick (every 0.1 s): when the assigned car gets a fault, leaves Normal mode, leaves the bank, or is no longer a member, the call goes to the best remaining car, and waits unassigned if there is none.

docs.title: 5b. Multiplayer
docs.text:
No signature in sections 1 to 5 changed. What is new is how they behave on a network client, plus one component and a few getters.

Server-authoritative cars. ALFElevator replicates (always relevant, no per-frame position). The server runs the state machine and writes a compact state (FLFElevatorNetState, internal): state, mode, fault, docked/target floor, the motion profile with its server start time, the door fraction and time of the last door change, lit calls (one bit per floor), load, light curtain, reset latch, the inspection views, and a small ring of the last 32 discrete events (state, mode, fault, arrival, departure, overload, obstruction, alarm) in the order the server raised them. A client rebuilds the motion and the doors from that state and the server clock (GetServerWorldTimeSeconds, smoothed so it never jumps), so a car moves smoothly between updates; a position jump after a late update (a fault stop arriving after a lost packet) is blended out over about 0.3 s. Also replicated: Preset, Configuration, bUseConfigurationOverride, ImportedParts, ElevatorId, BankName, DispatchBank, bShaftCollision, bStaticFixedParts (a change on the server rebuilds the car on every client, after the trip if it moves). The bank dispatches on the server only.

On a client, every command is sent to the server. ExecuteElevatorCommand, CallToFloor, SelectFloor, RequestHallCall, RequestDoorOpen/Close, SetOperatingMode, InjectFault, ResetFault, ResumeOperation, MaintenanceJog, the Toggle* functions, ALFElevatorBank::RequestHallCall/RequestDestination and ULFButtonComponent::PressButton do not change the client's copy: they send the request through the local player's ULFElevatorInteractorComponent. Their return value on a client means "sent" (the bank functions return null there). The press animation and button sound play at once on the client. PlayAlarm and PlayButtonSound stay local sounds. Cars with bReplicates turned off keep the single-player behaviour on every machine.

Events on clients. Every machine raises the elevator events for every car in the server's order (and so in the documented order of section 2): departure, the moving phases, arrival, door phases, mode, fault, overload, obstruction, and the alarm sound. The client replays the event ring, so several events that reach it in one update (the server sends at most its net rate) still come in the right order. When an update is lost, Unreal resends its properties later, so a newer update can arrive first: the client replays up to the missing entry and waits for the resend instead of skipping it. A client so far behind that the ring no longer reaches back takes the state as it is. OnPassengerEntered/Exited and GetOccupants stay local (each machine sees who stands in its cabin). Per-request events: the requesting client raises OnCommandExecuted and, when refused, OnCallRejected on its own copy when the server's answer comes back; a bank request raises OnAssigned or the bank's OnCallRejected on the requester's copy. Move Elevator To Floor works on clients too (a refusal arrives as an event). A client that joins late takes the current state as it is and raises only OnModeChanged, OnStateChanged and OnFaultChanged for values that differ from the defaults; nothing older is replayed.

ULFElevatorInteractorComponent (Runtime, player-owned). The server adds one to every player controller once a networked world has LiftForge cars (ULFElevatorSettings::bAutoAddInteractor, default on), or add it yourself to your PlayerController or pawn. Server-side checks on every request: AccessLevel (the server uses the lower of this and the level the caller asked for, so a client can lower but never raise its level), bAllowServiceCommands (off by default: only calls, doors, alarm and the help buttons), MaxRequestDistance (to the car's and shaft's bounds; 0, the default, turns the check off), MaxRequestsPerSecond (flood guard, default 20) and the overridable CanRunRequest. Functions: ExecuteElevatorCommand, CallToFloor, RequestHallCall, RequestDestination, PressButton (use them directly for split-screen), FindLocalInteractor, FindOrAddInteractor, event OnRequestCompleted. Set AccessLevel in your game mode's Post Login, as ALFDemoGameMode does (level 9 and service commands for every demo player).

Getters. ALFElevator::IsNetworkProxy and ALFElevatorBank::IsNetworkProxy (true on a client copy). On a client GetCurrentFloor ignores the short visual blend the client applies after a correction.

Inspection views are shared. Cutaway, labels and exploded view go through the server and change for every player (the exploded view also puts the car into Maintenance, which only the server can do). Setting bCutaway, bShowPartLabels or ExplodedAmount directly on a client copy is a local override that lasts until the server changes that view.

Server-side callers (AI). An AI controller or any server code calls CallToFloor, ExecuteElevatorCommand or ALFElevatorBank::RequestDestination on the server's actors directly, with its own access level, exactly as in single player; no interactor and no RPC are involved, and every client sees the result.

Riding. Generated components that a pawn can stand on (cabin floor, sills, shaft walls) have the same name on the server and every client and are network-addressable, so CharacterMovement can send the cabin floor as its movement base. Custom characters: see Using your own character; the important one is bStayBasedInAir = true on the CharacterMovement component.

docs.title: Elevator Builder
docs.text: The Elevator Builder is an editor tab that creates elevators from presets and lets you override anything. Open it from Tools > LiftForge > Elevator Builder. The tab is called LiftForge Builder.

docs.title: Create a car
docs.text:
1. Pick a preset in the builder.
  2. Choose Create. A new elevator actor is placed in the level and built from the preset. Undo removes it.

docs.title: Edit an existing car
docs.text:
1. Select an elevator actor in the level.
  2. Choose Use selected to load it into the builder.
  3. Enable Configuration Override on the actor (bUseConfigurationOverride). Without it the car follows its preset, and your edits to Configuration are ignored.
  4. Edit the Configuration in the Details panel (see below).
  5. Choose Rebuild to regenerate the geometry. A rebuild keeps your overrides and any components you added yourself. Only generated parts are regenerated.

Preview doors opens or closes the doors in the editor so you can check the opening without playing. Validate checks the configuration and lists any problems.

docs.title: What you can configure
docs.text:
All of these are properties of the configuration (FLFElevatorConfiguration). Lengths are in centimetres, speeds in cm/s.

Group Properties Identity Display name, Type (Passenger, Freight, Panoramic, Hydraulic, Platform, Cycle), Drive (gearless, geared, hydraulic), Door layout (centre opening, side sliding, telescopic, hinged) Floors Id, label, elevation, front and rear entrance, access level, announcement, for each landing. List floors from lowest to highest. Car and door size Cabin width, depth, height; door width and height Motion Max speed, max acceleration, max jerk Timing Door seconds, dwell seconds Load Capacity (kg), mass counted per pawn Dispatch Starvation seconds, direction change penalty seconds Look Visual set, or the four kit materials (cabin, door, floor, machinery); detail draw distance Sound Volume and one slot per sound; see Presets and visual sets Brand line Optional text printed on the car panel. Empty prints nothing.

Per actor you can also set ElevatorId, BankName / DispatchBank, Shaft Collision, Static Fixed Parts, and the inspection options. Details: API reference (ALFElevator).

docs.title: Rules the builder checks
docs.text:
Validate rejects a configuration (and an invalid car does not operate) when, for example:

  • there are no floors, or more than 128;
  • floor elevations are not sorted or are duplicated;
  • there are more floor buttons than fit beside the door (the panel grid grows for tall buildings, up to a limit);
  • imported parts are missing or malformed.

In the editor the problems go to the Message Log (Map Check) once per distinct problem, and an invalid actor shows a placeholder box with text instead of disappearing.

docs.title: Changing a car while playing
docs.text: You can change Preset, Configuration or ImportedParts at runtime. Then call Rebuild Assembly (geometry) or Mark Configuration Dirty (validation only). A preset swap or a changed floor count is also detected on the next tick. Calls to floors that no longer exist are dropped, and the car finds its landing again by floor id. A rebuild requested while the car moves runs when it arrives. The cabin floor component is kept, so riders stay on it.

docs.title: Large buildings
docs.text: Two to 128 floors are supported (one floor, or more than 128, is rejected with a message and the car does not operate). Cars with many floors get a fitted button grid beside the door. How many buttons fit depends on the cabin: a 220 cm wide cabin takes 40 floors, but a narrow ISO-sized cabin (135 cm wide with a 90 cm door) does not take 30. The validation message then says to widen the cabin, narrow the door or serve fewer floors. For tall buildings the instanced fixed parts keep the draw cost down; see Performance tips.

docs.title: Imported assemblies (advanced)
docs.text: ImportedParts lets you fit your own meshes instead of the generated kit: each part (FLFImportedPart) has a role (ELFImportedPartRole: CabinFloor, CabinRigid, CabinDoor, LandingFixed, LandingDoor, ShaftFixed), a transform, a floor id for landing roles and a collision flag. Validation requires centre-opening doors, unique part names, loadable meshes, exactly one colliding cabin floor and both colliding door leaves for every served entrance. After changing it from gameplay code, call Mark Configuration Dirty or Rebuild Assembly.

docs.title: Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons
docs.text:
The car operating panel has Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons. In 1.0 they are hooks only: pressing one is accepted and raises On Command Executed, and nothing else happens. What the button does in your project (play a voice line, open a UI, call a function, notify a server) is up to you.

The same event is raised after every command, so you bind once and filter by command.

docs.title: Bind in Blueprints
docs.text:
1. Get a reference to the elevator (for example from a level Blueprint or an actor that has the elevator as a variable).
  2. Drag from the elevator and choose Assign On Command Executed (in the Elevator > Events category).
  3. In the custom event, which receives Elevator, Command, Floor Id and Accepted, add a Switch on ELFElevatorCommand (or a == check).
  4. On Help, Phone or Emergency Call, run your own logic.

Do this in Begin Play so the binding exists before anyone presses a button. For many cars, bind each one when you spawn or find it.

docs.title: Bind in C++
docs.text:
// MyActor.h
UFUNCTION()
void HandleCommand(ALFElevator* Elevator, ELFElevatorCommand Command, FName FloorId, bool bAccepted);

// MyActor.cpp, for example in BeginPlay
Elevator->OnCommandExecuted.AddDynamic(this, &AMyActor::HandleCommand);

void AMyActor::HandleCommand(ALFElevator* Elevator, ELFElevatorCommand Command, FName FloorId, bool bAccepted)
{
    switch (Command)
    {
    case ELFElevatorCommand::EmergencyCall: /* alert the control room */ break;
    case ELFElevatorCommand::Help:          /* show help */ break;
    case ELFElevatorCommand::Phone:         /* start the intercom */ break;
    default: break;
    }
}

docs.title: Fire the buttons yourself
docs.text: Execute Elevator Command with EmergencyCall, Help or Phone raises the same event, so a UI button or a test can use the same path as a physical button press.

docs.title: Button names
docs.text:
A generated button stores its command as text so that levels saved with older versions keep working. The names never change: Select, Up, Down, Destination, Open, Close, Alarm, EmergencyCall, Help, Phone, Cutaway, Exploded, Labels, Overload, Obstruction, Normal, Independent, Maintenance, FireRecall, OutOfService, DoorJam, PowerLoss, EmergencyBrake, Stuck, Reset, Resume, JogUp, JogDown.

A button whose name is not in the list logs one warning when pressed and does nothing. If a custom button seems dead, check the Output Log for that warning. Use Set Command Type to choose a command from the enum instead of typing a name.
First release.

docs.title: Included
docs.text:
• Elevator actor with generated cabin, doors, landings, shaft and machinery, built from a preset or a configuration; Elevator Builder editor tab.
  • Nine presets with visual sets and Blueprints: Traction, MRL630, MRL1000, Goods2000, Bed2500, Panoramic, Hydraulic, Platform and Cycle.
  • Collective control, bank dispatch and destination dispatch, with bounded waiting and registration by name.
  • Five operating modes and four injectable faults, with overload and door-obstruction handling.
  • Inspection views: cutaway, exploded view and part labels; operator console and demo panel.
  • A frozen Blueprint API: two entry points, a command enum, door, call-rejection, overload, obstruction and passenger events, status getters and the latent Move Elevator To Floor node.
  • Multiplayer: server-authoritative cars that replicate to listen-server and dedicated-server clients, client requests through an interactor component with server-side access checks, and riding tested under emulated latency and packet loss. Clients replay every elevator event in the server's order, even after packet loss: a client waits for a resend instead of skipping an event. See the Multiplayer guide.
  • NPC riding: Elevator Nav Links for a plain Move To across floors, Behaviour Tree and StateTree tasks, the latent AI Ride Elevator node, polite queueing, bank and destination dispatch. See the NPC riding guide.
  • Desktop sample pawn and an OpenXR VR sample pawn (not tested on a real VR headset), using Enhanced Input.
  • Art: 291 authored part meshes (every preset with its own cabin, doors, frames and lift-type parts; 3 LODs, collision per part), 19 CC0 surface materials and 3 procedural sets, with 14 master materials, signage actors (ALFSignage: screens, posters, slideshows, media textures) with 35 sample images, cabin screens, and a mirror capture component for real cabin-mirror reflections.
  • Example maps LF_Showcase_Warm and LF_Showcase_Noir: two looks of one building core with a glazed double-height lobby, a passenger bank, a service corridor, alcoves, landings and a plant corridor, lit with Lumen and an HDRI.
  • Source code for the runtime, AI, demo and editor modules, with automation tests.

docs.title: Behaviour you may notice
docs.text:
• OnDoorsChanged(false) now fires after the state becomes Idle. Door events always follow the matching state change, so when a handler runs, the getters already show the new state. In 0.x builds the closed event fired first. If you used the event, check handlers that read the state.
  • Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons raise On Command Executed and do nothing else; see Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons.

  • A button with an unknown command name logs one warning and does nothing.

  • Elevator events now also fire on clients in multiplayer. Logic that must run once (NPCs, scoring, spawning) must check Has Authority.

  • The plugin enables the engine plugins StateTree and GameplayStateTree for NPC riding.
  • In multiplayer a character needs bStayBasedInAir; see Using your own character.
  • Out of Service lets passengers out: a moving car switched to Out of Service stops at the next floor, opens its doors once, closes them after the dwell and then accepts no calls.
  • In Maintenance mode the doors stay shut when a moving car stops at the next floor; Door Open still opens them.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: Within 1.x the names, parameter order and types of the documented API do not change, and enum values are only appended. New members are added with defaults. Removing or renaming a member is a major-version change.

docs.title: What is original
docs.text:
The meshes, sound effects and the three procedural texture sets are original work made with scripts. 20 surface materials and 2 HDRI skies are CC0 (public domain) files from ambientCG and Poly Haven, processed for this plugin. The signage images are drawn by the author with fictional or generic names.

Asset class How it was made Meshes Built from primitives with Blender Python. No scanned or downloaded geometry. Textures 19 CC0 surface materials (ambientCG, Poly Haven), resized and repacked. 3 procedural sets made by the author (numpy / PIL). 35 signage images drawn by the author. Sky 2 CC0 HDRI skies (Poly Haven). Materials 14 master materials and 105 material instances, authored in Unreal. Sound effects Synthesised (numpy / scipy), 48 kHz mono. Three MetaSound sources loop the motor, pump and door effects. Announcements AI-generated speech (see below). Fonts Noto Sans, Noto Serif (SIL OFL 1.1) and DejaVu (Bitstream Vera) were used to draw text into the signage images. No font file is shipped. Plugin icon Drawn by the author.

Dimensions are catalogue-neutral and no manufacturer's product is represented.
