docs.title: Standards
docs.text: Passenger, goods, bed, panoramic and hydraulic cars stay within the EN 81-20 maximum car area for their rated load. Sizes are visualisation sizes, inspired by common ISO 4190-1 classes, and catalogue-neutral. The platform and cycle lift sizes are illustrative. Check the standard and your jurisdiction for real projects. LiftForge is not affiliated with and not endorsed by any standards body.

docs.title: Bank and destination dispatch
docs.text: A bank (LFElevatorBank) dispatches hall and destination calls to a group of cars. A single car without a bank runs its own collective control.

docs.title: Set up a bank
docs.text:
1. Place an LFElevatorBank actor in the level.
  2. Link the cars. A car belongs to a bank in any of these ways, and they can be combined:
    • the bank lists the car in its Elevators array;
    • the car sets Dispatch Bank to the bank;
    • the car's Bank Name matches the bank's Bank Name;
    • you call Register Elevator on the bank at runtime.
  3. The link is two-way and automatic at BeginPlay. A car that names a bank is registered with it, and a bank registers every car it lists, so the car's hall buttons always reach the bank. Your authored Elevators array is never edited.
  4. Optionally place an LFOperatorConsole with the bank and an origin floor to get a destination keypad.

Check the setup with Validate Bank. In the editor the same checks appear in Map Check. It reports a bank with no cars, a car that belongs to another bank, a Bank Name conflict, two cars with the same ElevatorId, and a car that shares no floor with the others.

docs.title: Hall calls
docs.text: Request Hall Call (Origin Floor Id, Direction) on the bank returns the car with the shortest arrival estimate, or null and raises the bank's On Call Rejected. Calls are re-checked every 0.1 s: when the assigned car gets a fault, leaves Normal mode, leaves the bank, or is no longer a member, the call moves to the best remaining car, or waits unassigned if there is none.

docs.title: Destination calls
docs.text: Request Destination (Origin Floor Id, Destination Floor Id) picks a car, calls it to the origin and selects the destination when its doors open there. Matching journeys are grouped: a car that already carries a call with the same origin and destination gets Destination Grouping Bonus Seconds (default 15) taken off its estimate.

docs.title: How calls are served
docs.text:
Within one car, collective control de-duplicates cabin and directional hall requests and serves calls in the direction of travel first. Two settings keep that fair:

  • Starvation Seconds (default 30): a call older than this is served on the next trip.
  • Direction Change Penalty Seconds (default 10): added to a moving car's arrival estimate when it must reverse to serve a hall call.

A tie between cars is broken by the stable ElevatorId.

docs.title: Access levels
docs.text: Each floor has an Access Level. A call needs a caller level at or above the level of both the origin and the destination floor. AccessLevel is a parameter of the calls; the demo cabin buttons use level 0 and the operator panel uses 9. Your game decides which level a player has.

docs.title: Why was my call refused?
docs.text:
A refused call raises On Call Rejected with a reason (ELFCallRejectReason). Get Last Call Rejection returns the reason of the last call (None after an accepted one).

Reason Meaning Unknown Floor The car does not serve that floor. Same Floor Origin and destination are the same. Invalid Direction A hall call needs Up or Down, and not Up at the top or Down at the bottom. Access Denied The caller's level is below the floor's level. Fault Active A fault is active. Resume Required A fault was reset and the car waits for Resume. Out Of Service / Maintenance Mode / Fire Recall Mode The car is in that mode. Independent Service The car is in Independent mode and takes cabin calls only. Invalid Configuration The configuration is invalid, so the car does not operate. No Elevator Available The bank found no car for the call (bank only).

docs.title: Wait for a car in Blueprints
docs.text: Move Elevator To Floor (see Blueprint API) sends a car to a floor and waits. With a bank, use Request Destination on the bank so the bank picks the car.

docs.title: Bank and World Partition
docs.text: Use Bank Name instead of hard actor references when the cars and the bank live in different World Partition cells. See World Partition notes.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
I do not see any LiftForge assets. In the Content Browser open Settings and turn on Show Plugin Content. Also check Edit > Plugins that LiftForge is enabled.

The plugin does not load on my engine version. Use the download that matches your engine (5.6, 5.7 or 5.8). Plugin content saved in a newer engine does not open in an older one, so LiftForge content is authored in 5.6.

An example map is dark. The example maps have a post-process volume with manual exposure. A level without one uses auto exposure and can render very dark. Add a post process volume (unbound) and set the exposure to suit your scene.

docs.title: Cars do not behave
docs.text:
The car does not move when I press a button. Check, in this order:

  1. Validate the configuration (see Elevator Builder). An invalid car does not operate, and the problem is in the Message Log.
  2. The mode. Anything other than Normal discards calls, and a hall call is refused in Independent mode.
  3. A fault: Reset it and then Resume Operation.
  4. Overload: remove the extra load or Toggle Overload.
  5. Access level: Get Last Call Rejection gives the reason. See Bank and destination dispatch.

A custom button does nothing. Its command name is not in the list. The Output Log shows one warning for it. Use Set Command Type. See Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons.

Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons do nothing. That is by design in 1.0. They raise On Command Executed. See Help, Phone and Emergency Call buttons.

The doors reverse again and again. Something blocks the light curtain. Move it, or check Simulated Obstruction.

My Move Elevator To Floor node never finishes. It finishes on Arrived or Failed. Set a timeout so it cannot wait for ever, and check the Failed output: a mode change, a fault or a rejected call ends it.

My bank logs "no loaded cars". The cars are not linked or not loaded yet. See Bank and destination dispatch and World Partition notes.

docs.title: Riding
docs.text:
The camera shakes in the car (jitter). Single-player checks:

  • Ride on the cabin floor with a standard Character, or add LFRiderComponent to a pawn without CharacterMovement.
  • Do not teleport or move the character yourself while it stands in the car.
  • Do not rely on moving the elevator actor itself at runtime if Static Fixed Parts is on (it makes the root Static).

Multiplayer checks:

  • Turn on bStayBasedInAir on the CharacterMovement component and apply the other settings in Using your own character.
  • Do not move the car to a later tick group or drive it from a Timeline.
  • Do not change MaxWalkSpeed on the server and the client independently (for sprint, use a custom move flag).
  • Save the map before multiplayer Play In Editor.

My character falls through the car floor.

  • Check that the character's collision blocks the generated cabin parts (see Using your own character).
  • Leave Shaft Collision on so the character cannot enter the shaft from the side.

  • For a pawn without CharacterMovement, add a LFRiderComponent and give the pawn a collidable root.

  • In multiplayer, turn on bStayBasedInAir on the CharacterMovement component. A jump inside a moving car then stays relative to the car. See Using your own character.

My VR pawn falls through the car. Add a LFRiderComponent, use a collidable root, and keep the camera and controllers below a tracking-origin component. See VR setup.

docs.title: Packaging and cooking
docs.text:
Which assets are packaged? The assets that LiftForge needs without a preset pointing at them are soft references in DefaultLiftForge.ini, and the cooker packages them automatically. You do not need DirectoriesToAlwaysCook. The BP_LF_* Blueprints, presets and visual sets are packaged when something you ship references them.

Parts look wrong or use the default material in a packaged game. Instanced parts need materials with Used with Instanced Static Meshes enabled. All LiftForge materials have it. If you replaced a material, enable the flag on it. Cars fall back to ordinary components if any material in a group lacks it, so a missing flag costs performance but not correctness.

Parts show "unbuilt lighting". You turned on Static Fixed Parts in a project with static lighting. Build the lighting, or turn the option off.

Which platforms? Win64.

docs.title: Audio
docs.text:
How do I remove or replace the announcements? Clear the floor's Announcement slot and the Doors Opening / Doors Closing slots of the audio pack, or assign your own sound waves. The announcements are AI-generated; see Credits, licences and AI disclosure.

The sound is too loud or too quiet. Configuration.Audio.Volume (0.35 in the presets) scales the whole mix of one car. Apply Sound Mix in the LiftForge project settings controls the sound mix the cars push while they play.

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
Can I use LiftForge for a real lift design? No. It is a visualisation and simulation of behaviour, not a certified control system, and car sizes are visualisation sizes. See the note on the Overview.

Multiplayer: clients cannot use the cars. Save the map first: a level that was never saved cannot replicate level actors. Then check the player's interactor component and access level. See the Multiplayer guide.

Another player's character pops by the crouch height in a moving car (multiplayer). With packet loss, Unreal's character movement can show a remote player's crouch height before the capsule changes, for about one round trip. It corrects itself. See Multiplayer guide.

Another player's position jumps a little in multiplayer, or a multiplayer test fails once. Under packet loss, Unreal's character movement can correct a player's position: about 7 cm when jumping, and in rare cases up to about 50 cm when sprinting fast. This is engine behaviour; LiftForge does not change it. The test LiftForge.Network.PIE.ListenServer runs at 1 % emulated loss and can fail about 1 run in 10 for this reason. Run it once more before you report a bug. See Multiplayer guide.

My game logic runs once per player when a door opens. Elevator events now fire on clients too. Check Has Authority before gameplay or NPC logic.

NPCs do not ride. See the NPC riding guide.

docs.title: Inspection views
docs.text:
Inspection views show how a lift is built. Use them from the operator panel, from the physical operator console beside each car, or from Blueprints.

View Command What it does Cutaway Toggle Cutaway Hides the shaft wall on the side of the viewer so the car can be seen travelling. On by default (bCutaway). Exploded view Toggle Exploded View Moves the parts apart (ExplodedAmount from 0, assembled, to 1, fully exploded). Switching it on puts the car into Maintenance. Leaving Maintenance closes it. Part labels Toggle Part Labels Shows a text label on every part (bShowPartLabels). Labels are created the first time they are used.

From Blueprints call Toggle Cutaway, Toggle Exploded, Toggle Labels, or Execute Elevator Command with ToggleCutaway, ToggleExploded or ToggleLabels.

docs.title: Operator console and panel
docs.text: The LFOperatorConsole actor is a wall of physical buttons for one car: modes, faults, recovery, the inspection views, plus a floor or destination keypad and a status line. Assign its Elevator, optionally its Bank (destination calls then go through the bank) and the Origin Floor Id it stands on. Use Rebuild Console after you change it. The demo's UMG panel (key H) offers the same commands in the same order.

docs.title: Camera enclosure tag
docs.text: The example maps hide lobby walls, lintels and ceilings in their inspection cameras by the actor tag LiftForgeInspectionEnclosure. Tag your own walls with it if you build review cameras that should look into the building.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The exploded view moves static parts too. If you build with Static Fixed Parts, the exploded view switches them to Movable.
  • Cutaway hides geometry, not collision. For a walk-through leave Shaft Collision on so nobody walks into the shaft.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Item Requirement Engine Unreal Engine 5.6, 5.7 or 5.8. Download the plugin build that matches your engine version. Platform Windows 64-bit (Win64). C++ toolchain Only if you build the plugin yourself or your project already has C++ code. Use the toolchain your engine version asks for. Plugins used Enhanced Input, MetaSounds, XRBase, StateTree and GameplayStateTree (all shipped with the engine; the last two are for NPC riding). OpenXR is optional and only needed for headsets.

The three MetaSound sources need the MetaSounds plugin, which the plugin enables for you. Epic's guide: https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/metasounds-quick-start

docs.title: Install from Fab
docs.text:
1. Open the Epic Games Launcher, go to Fab in your library and find LiftForge.
  2. Choose Install to Engine for the engine version you use (check the wording in your launcher version). Fab provides one download per engine version.
  3. Restart the editor, open Edit > Plugins, search for LiftForge and make sure it is enabled.
  4. If you build your own project from source, regenerate the project files and compile once. Plugin binaries are built by Epic for the versions Fab lists.

Installing LiftForge as an engine plugin has been proven on UE 5.6 only.

docs.title: Install by hand (project plugin)
docs.text: Copy the LiftForge folder into your project's Plugins folder (create it if needed), so you have YourProject/Plugins/LiftForge/LiftForge.uplugin. Open the project. If Unreal asks to rebuild modules, accept. A manual copy has no compiled code, so it needs Visual Studio with C++ so Unreal can build it. Without them, install from Fab.

docs.title: Show the plugin content
docs.text:
In the Content Browser open Settings and enable Show Plugin Content. The LiftForge content is under LiftForge Content:

Folder Contents Presets DA_Preset_<Key> data assets, one per preset VisualSets DA_VisualSet_<Key> data assets Blueprints BP_LF_<Key> ready-to-place elevators Materials Master materials (Masters) and material instances (Instances) Meshes Kit and HQ meshes Textures Surface maps, signage images and HDRI cubemaps Audio Sound waves, three MetaSound sources, attenuation and sound mix Input Enhanced Input assets used by the demo pawns Examples/Maps LF_Showcase_Warm and LF_Showcase_Noir, the example maps Examples/AI The sample NPC (BP_LF_SampleNPC)

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text:
LiftForge needs no project settings to run. Optional settings live under Project Settings > Plugins:

  • LiftForge: the assets every car uses when a preset does not point at its own (kit meshes, kit materials, LED materials, sound attenuation, sound mix), Apply Sound Mix and the parked-car tick interval. Changes are saved to your project's Config/DefaultLiftForge.ini. The cooker packages these assets automatically, so you do not need a "Directories to always cook" entry.
  • LiftForge Demo: Apply VR Performance CVars, the VR laser material and the Input Config asset. See VR setup and Using your own character.

docs.title: Check the install
docs.text: Open /LiftForge/Examples/Maps/LF_Showcase_Warm and press Play. You stand in a lobby with a bank of passenger cars. Walk up to a button and press it. If something is missing, see FAQ and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Set a mode with Set Operating Mode, or with the Mode... commands of Execute Elevator Command. Any mode other than Normal discards the queued calls.

Mode What the car does Normal Automatic collective control: serves hall and cabin calls. Independent Attendant service: serves cabin calls only. Hall calls are rejected (Independent Service). Maintenance Inspection service: no calls. The car moves only with Maintenance Jog (next floor up or down), starting with the doors closed. The doors open at the end of a jog, the only Maintenance stop where they open on their own. Fire Recall Fire service phase 1: the car returns to the recall floor and opens its doors there. Normal calls are cleared. Out of Service The car accepts no calls. A moving car stops at the next floor it can reach and opens its doors once so passengers can get out.

docs.title: Changing the mode while the car moves
docs.text:
A moving car does not stop dead. Maintenance and Out of Service brake the car to the next floor it can stop at within its acceleration limit, with no jump in velocity. Fire Recall does the same when the car is moving away from the recall floor, keeps the doors shut on the way, then returns to the recall floor and opens its doors.

In Maintenance the car stops at the next reachable floor and keeps its doors closed. The Door Open button and command still open them, so nobody is trapped. In Out of Service, a car that was moving stops at the next reachable floor and opens its doors once, so passengers can get out. It closes them after the normal dwell time and then accepts no calls. While those doors are still open or closing, Door Open and the door sensor reopen them as usual; once they are fully shut, Door Open is refused until the car leaves Out of Service. A car that is already standing still when switched to Out of Service is unchanged. Fire Recall is as described above.

docs.title: Faults
docs.text:
Faults let you test how your project reacts. Start one with Inject Fault or the Fault... commands.

Fault Effect Door Jam The doors cannot open or close. Power Loss The car stops and the cabin lights go out. Emergency Brake The emergency brake dropped. Stuck Between Floors The car stopped between two floors.

A fault discards the queued calls and stops the car. While any fault is active, door commands are rejected. Reset Fault clears the fault and holds the car (state Stopped). While the car is held, Door Open is also refused. Reset never restarts travel by itself: call Resume Operation to continue. At a floor the car carries on; between floors it travels to the nearest floor. Reset Fault does nothing when there is no fault, and Resume Operation does nothing when the car is not held.

docs.title: Overload and door obstruction
docs.text:
• Overload: the load of the cabin is the sum of the actors inside it. A pawn counts Passenger Mass Kg (75 by default) unless it has a LFLoadComponent with its own mass. Other actors count through that component or their physics-body mass. Above the capacity the car does not travel, and On Overload Changed fires. Toggle Overload simulates a load one passenger above the capacity.
  • Door light curtain: something in the doorway blocks the doors. Closing doors reverse and reopen, and On Obstruction Changed fires. Toggle Obstruction simulates a blocked curtain. The curtain is only read while the doors are not fully closed or while something is bound to the event.

docs.title: Status and events
docs.text: Read the state with Get State, Get Operating Mode and Get Fault, or bind to On State Changed, On Mode Changed and On Fault Changed. Events fire in a fixed order; see Blueprint API.

docs.title: Not a certified controller
docs.text: These behaviours illustrate how lifts react. They are not a certified control-system model. In particular fire service, inspection and fault handling are simplified for visualisation.

docs.title: Multiplayer guide
docs.text: LiftForge cars are server-authoritative. The server runs the state machine, and every client shows the same car, doors, displays and sounds. This page covers setup, what clients can do, how riding works over a network, and what to check when something looks wrong.

docs.title: 1. What is replicated
docs.text:
• The car's state. The server writes a compact state: state, mode, fault, docked and target floor, the motion profile with its server start time, the door fraction and time of the last door change, lit calls, load, light curtain, the reset latch and the inspection views. The position is not sent every frame: clients rebuild the motion and the doors from that state and the server clock, so a car moves smoothly between updates.
  • Events, in the server's order. The server also sends a ring of its last 32 discrete events (state, mode, fault, arrival, departure, overload, obstruction, alarm). A client replays them in order, so even when several events arrive in one update, handlers see the documented order (see Blueprint API) and the sounds, chimes and announcements play on every client. After a lost packet a client waits for the resend instead of skipping an event.
  • Configuration. Preset, Configuration, bUseConfigurationOverride, ImportedParts, bShaftCollision, bStaticFixedParts, ElevatorId, BankName and DispatchBank replicate. A change on the server rebuilds the car on every client (after the trip, if the car is moving). A car spawned at runtime by the server therefore also exists on clients.
  • The bank. It replicates, so a bank spawned at runtime exists on clients, but it dispatches on the server only.

A car replicates by default (bReplicates). A car with replication turned off keeps the single-player behaviour on every machine.

docs.title: 2. Set up a multiplayer project
docs.text:
1. Save the map before you test. A map that was never saved ("Untitled") cannot replicate level actors by name, so clients cannot find the cars. Save the level first, then use Play In Editor with several players.
  2. Nothing else is required on the elevator or the bank. There is no checkbox to tick: cars replicate and the server dispatches.
  3. Players need the interactor component. The server adds a LFElevatorInteractorComponent to every player controller once a networked world has LiftForge cars. This is the setting bAutoAddInteractor in the LiftForge settings, on by default. If you prefer, add the component to your PlayerController or pawn yourself and turn the setting off.
  4. Set each player's access level in your game mode's Post Login (see section 3). The demo game mode gives every player level 9 and allows service commands.
  5. For a custom character, apply the settings in Using your own character.

The demo game mode of the example maps already does steps 3 and 4. A VR pawn works for single player and for the listen host; for multiplayer VR, use a Character-based pawn (section 4).

docs.title: 3. Calling and operating cars from a client
docs.text:
On a client, every command is sent to the server instead of changing the local copy. This covers Execute Elevator Command, Call To Floor, Select Floor, Request Hall Call, Request Door Open / Close, Set Operating Mode, Inject Fault, Reset Fault, Resume Operation, Maintenance Jog, the Toggle... functions, the bank's Request Hall Call and Request Destination, and Press Button. You use the same nodes as in single player.

  • Return values. On a client the return value of these functions means "sent", not "accepted". The bank functions return null there.
  • Answer events. The player who sent the request hears the answer on its own copy of the car: On Command Executed, or On Call Rejected when the server refused it. For a bank request, On Assigned or the bank's On Call Rejected. Move Elevator To Floor also works on clients; a refusal arrives as an event.
  • Instant feedback. The button press animation and sound play at once on the client. Play Alarm and Play Button Sound stay local sounds.

docs.title: The interactor component and access levels
docs.text:
LFElevatorInteractorComponent lives on the player. It sends the request and the server decides, with these checks:

Check Meaning AccessLevel The server uses the lower of this level and the level the caller asked for. A client can lower its level, never raise it. bAllowServiceCommands Off (the default): only calls, doors, the alarm and the help buttons are accepted. MaxRequestDistance How near the player must be to the car and its shaft. 0, the default, turns the distance check off. MaxRequestsPerSecond Flood guard, 20 by default. CanRunRequest An overridable function for your own rules.

Service commands are off by default. A player can make calls, work the doors and press the alarm and help buttons. Modes, faults, reset, resume, jog, the inspection views and the simulated load and obstruction are refused until you set bAllowServiceCommands to true on that player's interactor. Turn it on only for players who may stop or fault a car. The demo game mode turns it on for every player.

Set AccessLevel in your game mode's Post Login. The component also has Execute Elevator Command, Call To Floor, Request Hall Call, Request Destination and Press Button, which you can call directly (for example for split-screen), plus Find Local Interactor, Find Or Add Interactor and the event On Request Completed.

docs.title: 4. Riding in multiplayer
docs.text:
Characters ride as they do in single player: the cabin floor is their movement base. LiftForge gives the cabin floor and the sills the same name on the server and on every client and makes them network-addressable, so CharacterMovement can send them as the base. Your character needs a few settings, listed in Using your own character. The one that matters most is bStayBasedInAir = true on the CharacterMovement component.

Tested results with a listen server and with a dedicated server, 2 clients each, 50 ms each way (100 ms round trip) and 1 % packet loss each way, on UE 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8:

  • The car's height on a client differed from the server's by at most 0.027 cm at the same server time in normal runs; one run of 15 measured 1.3 cm during a server frame hitch.
  • A rider standing in the car showed steady height above the floor and a largest frame-to-frame step of 0.010 cm. No fall-through: the lowest point after a jump landing was above the floor.
  • A jump inside a moving car reached the same height as in a still room.
  • Riding, crouching and walking in and out produced almost no corrections. Under packet loss, Unreal's character movement can correct a player's position: about 7 cm when jumping, and in rare cases up to about 50 cm when sprinting fast. This is engine behaviour; LiftForge does not change it. In the same test setup, a jump gave a correction of 6.5 to 6.7 cm (4 times in 90 runs), and sprinting at 6 m/s gave corrections of 8 to 54 cm (5 times in 140 runs).
  • A car moving at 5 m/s was tested with a jump at speed.

These numbers come from the automated tests on the author's PC, with 2 clients in one editor process; your network will differ. Multiplayer has not been tested over a real network or by human players.

docs.title: 5. Late joiners and relevancy
docs.text:
• The car is always relevant: it exists on every client regardless of distance, and it sends no per-frame position, so tall shafts need no relevancy tuning.
  • A client that joins mid-trip takes the current state as it is: it sees the car where it is, moving, with the right displays and mode. It does not replay old events (no old chimes). It raises only the mode, state and fault events for values that differ from the defaults.
  • The first state is applied once the client's network clock is valid, so a late joiner does not see a jump.
  • A client that reconnects while a car travels was tested.

docs.title: 6. Inspection views over the network
docs.text: Cutaway, part labels and the exploded view are shared: they go through the server and change for every player. On a client they are service commands, so that player needs bAllowServiceCommands (section 3). The exploded view also puts the car in Maintenance mode, which only the server can do. Setting the cutaway, labels or exploded amount directly on a client's copy is a local override that lasts until the server changes that view.

docs.title: 7. Events and the data that stays local
docs.text:
• Elevator events fire on clients too. Every machine raises the elevator events (departure, the moving phases, arrival, door phases, mode, fault, overload, obstruction, alarm) for every car, in the server's order. Logic that must run once, such as NPC and gameplay logic, scoring, spawning, must check Has Authority first, or it will run once per machine.
  • Stays local per machine: Occupants, On Passenger Entered / Exited (each machine sees who stands in its own cabin).
  • Per request: the requesting client raises On Command Executed and On Call Rejected on its own copy when the answer comes back.
  • Getters. Is Network Proxy (on the car and on the bank) is true on a client copy. On a client, Get Current Floor ignores the short visual blend the client applies after a correction.

docs.title: 8. Test checklist
docs.text:
Run these with Play > Advanced Settings > Multiplayer Options: first Play As Listen Server with 3 players, then Play As Client with 2 players (a dedicated server). Turn on Run Under One Process, and Network Emulation for everyone with a custom profile of 50 ms each way and 1 % packet loss. Save the map first. Tick everything in both rounds.

  • Hall call from a client: the car comes on every screen at the same time, and chimes play near the car on every client.
  • Cabin call from a rider: the button animates at once, the LED lights on every screen, the car leaves after the doors close.
  • Destination call at a console: the bank assigns a car and the status shows it.
  • A floor above the player's access level: the press animates, no LED lights, the car does not go.
  • Two clients call the same car at once: both calls are served.
  • Ride up and down, with two players watching each other: no shaking, no sinking, level arrival.
  • Jump while the car accelerates, cruises and brakes: you land on the floor, no snap back.
  • Crouch while riding. Sprint out as the doors open.
  • Fault while a car carries a rider: the car stops at the same height on every screen, the alarm sounds, the rider stays on the floor. Reset, then Resume.
  • Fire recall while a car travels away: it stops at the next floor with the doors shut, returns and opens.
  • Maintenance with a jog; out of service while moving.
  • Overload toggle; stand in the doorway; passenger alarm.
  • Cutaway, exploded view, labels from a client: every screen changes.
  • Join a new client mid-trip, during a fault, and during a fire recall.
  • A client disconnects while riding.
  • Logs: no LogLiftForge errors, no "has no LFElevatorInteractorComponent" warning, and no warnings about unresolved or unmapped elevator components.

p.NetShowCorrections 1 in a client console shows every movement correction; there should be almost none. Under packet loss, expect a few (see section 9).

Automation test under packet loss. LiftForge.Network.PIE.ListenServer runs with 1 % emulated packet loss. For the reason above it can fail about 1 run in 10. If it fails, run it once more before you report a bug. The failures are movement corrections of more than 5 cm, not a fault in the elevator.

docs.title: 9. Known limits
docs.text:
• Not tested over a real network or by human players (section 4).
  • Server and Client build targets were not compiled. The launcher engine cannot build them, so dedicated-server behaviour was tested in the editor only.
  • Server only for commands that change a car. Clients send requests; the server decides. A client cannot raise its own access level.
  • VR pawn. The demo VR pawn is single player and listen host only, and it has not been tested on a real VR headset; its VR switch needs authority. For multiplayer VR, use a Character-based pawn.
  • Occupants and passenger events are local per machine.
  • Never-saved maps cannot replicate level actors.
  • Remote crouch on a moving car under packet loss. The crouch flag of a character replicates apart from its movement. If the packet with the flag is lost, another player's character riding a moving car shows its new height with the old capsule until the resend: a pop of up to the crouch height difference (about 28 cm with the default capsule) for about one round trip. This is how Unreal replicates crouch for other players' characters, not LiftForge, and it corrects itself.
  • Movement corrections under packet loss. Under packet loss, Unreal's character movement can correct a player's position: about 7 cm when jumping, and in rare cases up to about 50 cm when sprinting fast. This is engine behaviour; LiftForge does not change it.
  • Corrections right after you teleport a player into or out of a car are expected.
  • Pawns without CharacterMovement ride through LFRiderComponent, which carries the pawn on each machine but does not replicate its movement.

docs.title: 10. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
I press a button on a client and nothing happens. Check that the world has cars when the player joined (the interactor is added by the server), that bAutoAddInteractor is on or you added the component, and the player's access level. The log warns when a player has no interactor component.

Clients cannot name the car, or the car does not appear. You played in an unsaved map. Save the level and try again.

Jitter or snapping on clients while riding. Check that the character has bStayBasedInAir on, that you did not move the car to a later tick group or drive it from a Timeline, and that you do not change MaxWalkSpeed on the server and the client independently (for sprint, use the usual custom move flag).

Another player pops up and down by about 28 cm when crouching in a moving car. See the known limits: with packet loss, Unreal shows the new height before the capsule until the crouch flag is resent. It corrects itself after about one round trip.

A client falls through the floor when jumping in a moving car. Turn on bStayBasedInAir on the CharacterMovement component. See Using your own character.

My game logic runs several times when a door opens. The door events fire on every machine now. Check Has Authority before gameplay logic.

An NPC rides on the server but I do not see it on a client. NPC riding runs on the server only. Clients see NPCs through normal Character replication. See the NPC riding guide.

docs.title: NPC riding guide
docs.text:
LiftForge can let AI characters use cars on their own: they call the car, wait politely, board, press their floor, ride and get out. There are two ways to use it: add navigation links and use a plain Move To, or call a ride task from a Behaviour Tree, a StateTree or a Blueprint.

The sample NPC and the NPC demo described in section 10 are part of the LF_Showcase_Warm and LF_Showcase_Noir maps: press Play and watch the first three cars.

docs.title: 1. What NPC riding does
docs.text:
The NPC code is a separate module, LiftForgeAI, so the core runtime stays free of AI dependencies. The plugin enables the engine plugins StateTree and GameplayStateTree for it.

A ride goes through five phases:

  1. Approaching. The NPC walks to a waiting spot beside the landing door. Far landings use the AI controller's pathfinding when there is a navigation mesh.
  2. Waiting. The NPC stands at its waiting spot and presses the call button again every 2 seconds while no serving car stands open there. If a crowd pushes it into the light curtain, it boards on its turn or steps straight out.
  3. Boarding. The NPC walks in along the door axis, once the doors have been open for a short moment and nobody is getting out.
  4. Riding. The NPC presses its floor, stands on a free cabin spot clear of the doors and turns to the door it will leave by.
  5. Exiting. The NPC walks out along the door axis and to a spot beside the door.

A ride runs on the server only. See section 9.

docs.title: 2. Ways to make an NPC ride
docs.text:
Way Where Result Elevator Nav Links (component) Add to a placed car A plain Move To across floors works. Pathfinding plans through the car, the AI rides and walks on. Ride Elevator To Floor (Behaviour Tree task) Behaviour Trees Succeeds when the pawn is out of the car on the floor, fails otherwise. Ride Elevator To Floor (StateTree task, category LiftForge) StateTrees Running while riding, Succeeded or Failed at the end. AI Ride Elevator (latent Blueprint node) Any Blueprint Exec pins Arrived and Failed. Exactly one fires, once.

All of them drive the same component, Elevator Ride (LFElevatorRideComponent). It is added to the pawn automatically; place it yourself to tune it.

docs.title: 3. Navigation links (a plain Move To)
docs.text:
1. Select a placed car and Add Component > Elevator Nav Links.
  2. Rebuild navigation (Build > Build Paths) and save the map. Link ids are generated in the editor and saved with the component, so a navigation mesh built in the editor finds its links in a cooked game.
  3. Use a normal Move To to a point on another floor. The path goes through the car: the link pauses the move, runs a ride, lets the pawn out exactly at the link end and resumes the move. A failed ride aborts the move, and the AI's Move To fails so your logic can re-plan.

Setup notes:

  • Put a NavMeshBoundsVolume around every landing of every floor, plus about 2 m. Agent radius 34 to 42 cm and agent height at least 180 cm are suitable. A static navigation mesh is fine: the links are baked.
  • The component makes one link per pair of floors, in both directions, between landing points LandingDistance (120 cm) out from the landing doors. Keep the landing walkable at least that far.
  • Link cost is the vertical distance plus an entering cost (600, about six metres of walking, for the wait). Short hops prefer stairs where there are any.
  • Keep bExcludeCabinFromNavigation on (default). In game, the cabin parts and landing door leaves then stop affecting navigation, so a runtime-built navigation mesh is not rebuilt while the car moves.
  • After you change floors at runtime, call Refresh Links.
  • Availability. Links of a car that cannot serve (a fault, any mode other than Normal; for a bank, when no member can serve) are skipped by new path queries.
  • Access levels. A link to or from a floor with an access level is used only by an AI whose Elevator Ride component has Default Access Level at least that level (staff, guards). For everyone else pathfinding finds another way, or none. DefaultAccessLevel is 0 by default and is also the level of rides that links start.

Properties: LinkAreaClass, LandingDistance, CallMode, RideTimeoutSeconds, bExcludeCabinFromNavigation, SupportedAgents. Functions: Get Elevator, Get Link Count, Refresh Links.

docs.title: 4. Behaviour Tree
docs.text:
Add the task Ride Elevator To Floor to a sequence. It succeeds when the pawn is out of the car on the floor and fails otherwise; aborting the task cancels the ride.

Option Meaning ElevatorKey An object key holding a car or a bank. Empty: the nearest car that serves the floor. DestinationFloor or DestinationFloorKey The floor, as a fixed value or a name key. AccessLevel The access level used for the ride. CallMode See section 7. TimeoutSeconds 0 for no limit.

A minimal tree: Sequence [ Ride Elevator To Floor (destination floor key), Move To (room) ].

docs.title: 5. StateTree
docs.text:
Add the task Ride Elevator To Floor (category LiftForge) to a state of a StateTree that uses the schema "StateTree AI Component". Inputs: Pawn (binds automatically to the AI schema's actor), an optional ElevatorOrBank, and parameters DestinationFloor, AccessLevel, CallMode, TimeoutSeconds. Outputs: Failure and RejectReason. The task is Running while it rides and finishes with Succeeded or Failed; leaving the state cancels the ride.

A minimal tree: Idle (Delay) → Ride (task) → Walk (Move To).

docs.title: 6. Blueprint node
docs.text:
AI Ride Elevator is a latent node. Exec pins: Arrived (Rider, Elevator, Floor Id) and Failed (Rider, Elevator, Failure, Reject Reason). Exactly one fires, once. Cancel ends the ride with Cancelled.

The failure is a ELFRideFailure: InvalidRequest, CallRejected, ServiceUnavailable, Interrupted, Blocked (could not reach the landing, the car or the exit in time, or could not board within BoardStallSeconds), TimedOut, Cancelled, ElevatorDestroyed. For CallRejected the second output is the ELFCallRejectReason.

If you want to drive the ride yourself, use the Elevator Ride component: Start Ride (elevator, destination floor, origin floor, access level, call mode, timeout), Cancel Ride, and the events On Ride Arrived, On Ride Failed and On Ride Phase Changed, with status getters (Is Riding, Get Ride Phase, and so on).

docs.title: 7. Queueing, doors, load and faults
docs.text:
Queueing and doors

  • Waiting spots alternate left and right of the door, and are placed clear of the light curtain.
  • People get out first. A rider waits until the doors have been open for BoardDelaySeconds, the curtain is free and no rider getting off at this floor is still inside. A player, or a pawn without the Elevator Ride component, counts only while it stands in the door curtain, so an NPC can board while such a pawn is still inside.
  • One rider goes through the door at a time, and first come boards first.
  • On the way out, the rider nearest the door goes first and presses Door Open if the doors start closing.
  • A rider that is not yet in the doorway gives up boarding when the doors start to close: an NPC does not wait in the doorway. Riders inside stand clear of the curtain, so the doors close after the normal dwell.

Load. A rider boards only when the car's load, the riders already walking in and its own mass fit the capacity, and a free cabin spot exists. Otherwise it lets the car go and waits for the next one. A rider counts its LFLoadComponent mass, or the car's Passenger Mass Kg. A 220 × 240 cm cabin takes 4 NPCs of radius 34 cm; extra NPCs take the next car, even when the capacity would allow more.

Banks and call modes. Set CallMode on the task, the component or the links:

  • Hall Call (default). The NPC presses the landing button for its direction and the destination inside. With a bank, the call goes through the bank and the NPC takes any member car that opens for its direction. With destination dispatch the NPC boards only the car the bank assigned.
  • Destination Dispatch. The NPC asks the bank for its destination and boards only the assigned car. Without a bank, it calls the car with Call To Floor.
  • This Car Only. The call goes to this car even when it belongs to a bank. This also rides a car in Independent mode when an attendant opens it.

Rejections and faults. These end the ride at once: unknown floor, same floor, invalid direction, access denied, invalid configuration. Any other refusal, or a car that stops serving (fault, out of service, maintenance, fire recall, independent service, resume required), is waited out for ServiceWaitSeconds (60 by default), then the ride fails with Service Unavailable (outside the car) or Interrupted (inside). If the car opens its doors while it is not serving the trip (Out of Service letting passengers out, fire recall), the rider gets out there and the ride ends Interrupted with the reason. In a Maintenance stop the doors stay shut, so a rider inside presses Door Open, gets out, and the ride ends Interrupted.

Characters and other pawns. Characters ride on the cabin floor as their movement base. The component steers them with movement input. Other pawns (no CharacterMovement) are carried by the component while inside.

Tuning (defaults, on the Elevator Ride component): AcceptanceRadius 25 cm, WaitDistance 70 cm, WaitSideClearance 35 cm, ExitDistance 170 cm, BoardDelaySeconds 1.2, BoardStallSeconds 45, FaceDoorDegreesPerSecond 270, BoardTimeoutSeconds 8, ApproachTimeoutSeconds 60, ExitTimeoutSeconds 10, ServiceWaitSeconds 60, RetryIntervalSeconds 2, MoveInputScale 1, bUseNavigationToApproach on, DefaultAccessLevel 0.

docs.title: 8. What you can use without the NPC module
docs.text: An AI pawn can also use a car with the public API alone: Call To Floor, the latent Move Elevator To Floor node, the door and obstruction events, Get Occupants, the call-rejection reason, and Request Destination on a bank. The NPC module adds the walking, queueing and boarding on top of these. See Blueprint API and Bank and destination dispatch.

docs.title: 9. Multiplayer
docs.text:
Riding is server only. Start Ride on a client logs a warning and fails with Invalid Request. NPCs call the car on the server's actors directly with their own access level: no interactor component, no network request. Clients see NPCs through normal Character replication and see the cars through the replicated state.

Check Has Authority before running NPC decision logic. The elevator events now also fire on clients. See the Multiplayer guide. Give NPC characters bStayBasedInAir if they can jump.

docs.title: 10. The example NPCs in the showcase maps
docs.text:
Each example map has six sample NPCs that walk between the floors and ride the cars on their own. Press Play and watch the first three cars.

  • The NPC. LiftForge Content/Examples/AI/BP_LF_SampleNPC is a Blueprint of LiftForge Sample NPC (ALFSampleNPC, a Character with an Elevator Ride component, UE's default 34 x 88 cm capsule and a simple body mesh). Its controller, LiftForge Sample NPC Controller, waits 2 to 6 seconds, picks a target point on another floor and walks there with a plain Move To. The cars do the rest through their Elevator Nav Links. It does not use a Behaviour Tree or a StateTree, so you can see that no elevator logic is needed in the AI.
  • The cars. The Traction car and the two MRL cars carry the Elevator Nav Links component. The Traction car and the first MRL car use hall calls; the second MRL car uses destination dispatch.
  • The places. Thirteen target points (tag LiftForgeNPCTarget) stand on the landings in front of those cars.
  • Navigation. A navigation bounds volume covers the three lobbies and a RecastNavMesh actor with Runtime Generation = Dynamic builds the mesh when the level starts, so nothing baked can go out of date.
  • Multiplayer. The map has four player starts, so a listen server with several clients works at once (Play > Number of Players 2+, Net Mode Play As Listen Server). The NPCs run on the server only. In the release check (a listen server and two clients, 100 ms round trip, 1 % packet loss, UE 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8), NPCs riding a moving car stayed on its floor on both clients: the largest frame-to-frame change of an NPC's height above the cabin floor was 0.7 cm, and the spread over a ride under 1.6 cm.
  • Known limit. In a test on the Warm map (6 runs of 170 s), 4 of 46 rides of the sample NPCs ended with Blocked while the rider was getting out of the car. The cause is not known. Your own logic should expect a Blocked result and give the NPC a new goal.

The sample NPC uses the defaults of the Elevator Ride component and the engine's default Character capsule (34 x 88 cm). It is not shrunk to fit. The showcase lobby walls stand 46 cm in front of the landing doors, with an opening only 30 cm wider than the door. A rider finds its way there without tuning: when the waiting spot (or the way from it to the door) would touch level geometry, the Elevator Ride component moves the spot out in steps of 10 cm, up to 150 cm, until a pawn of its size fits and can walk sideways to the door axis and straight in; it then lines up with the door before it enters, instead of cutting the corner of the wall. Static and dynamic level geometry counts; other pawns and the car itself do not. Wait Distance is the starting point of that search, so you rarely need to change it; raise it yourself if your recess is deeper than 1.5 m or you want the riders to stand further back.

docs.title: Character size and door width
docs.text:
A rider fits a car when its capsule is narrower than the door: 2 x radius + 6 cm must not exceed the clear door width (Door Width of the configuration). The release check (LiftForge.Content.StandardCharacterRides) puts a plain Character in front of each of the nine showcase cars and rides it from the first to the second floor:

Preset Door width Largest radius (rule) 34 x 88 (UE default) 42 x 96 Traction, MRL 1000, Panoramic, Hydraulic, Platform 90 cm 42 cm rides rides MRL 630, Cycle 80 cm 37 cm rides does not fit (84 cm capsule, 80 cm door) Bed 2500 130 cm 62 cm rides rides Goods 2000 140 cm 67 cm rides rides

The cabin spots also depend on the radius: a 110 x 140 cm cabin (MRL 630) has room for one rider of radius 34 cm clear of the door light curtain, so a second NPC takes the next car. If your character is wider than the door of a preset, widen Door Width (and the cabin) of your configuration; the NPC module does not squeeze a capsule through a door.

To build your own: a Character with an AI controller, an Elevator Nav Links component on every car, a navigation bounds volume over the landings, and a Behaviour Tree that does Move To to a point on another floor, or the Ride Elevator To Floor task, or the AI Ride Elevator node.

docs.title: 11. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
NPCs never use the elevator. Check that the Elevator Nav Links component is on the car, that navigation was rebuilt after you added it, that the link ends are on the navigation mesh (check LandingDistance), and that the car is in Normal mode without a fault.

The NPC waits for ever. The car may not serve the floor or direction. Check ServiceWaitSeconds, BoardStallSeconds and whether someone stands in the door. With BoardStallSeconds at 0 a rider that cannot board waits for ever.

The NPC stands next to the door. Something stands on the waiting spots or in front of the door. The ride steers straight in the lobby and does not path-find around people. Keep 2 m beside and 3 m in front of the doors free, and have the sample NPC walk away after it arrives.

The navigation mesh rebuilds while the car moves. Keep bExcludeCabinFromNavigation on.

The NPC refuses a floor. It is access denied: raise the NPC's DefaultAccessLevel or the task's access level. The failure reads Call Rejected with the reason Access Denied.

The NPC does not ride to the right floor. Check the destination floor id and that the car serves it (Get Floors). Unknown floors fail at once with Invalid Request.

docs.title: Using your own character
docs.text: The demo character and VR pawn are samples. You do not need them. Any pawn can ride a car and press its buttons.

docs.title: How riding works
docs.text:
• Characters (CharacterMovement). The cabin has a floor component (Get Cabin Floor returns it). A character standing on it moves with the car through CharacterMovement's normal moving-base handling. You do not add anything to the character for this.
  • Other pawns (a VR pawn, a vehicle, a custom pawn without CharacterMovement). Add a LFRiderComponent. It looks below the owner for a cabin floor (Floor Probe Distance, 120 cm by default) and carries the pawn with it. The pawn needs a collidable root, and cameras and controllers should sit below a tracking-origin component.
  • The cabin floor component is kept when the car rebuilds, so riders stay based on it.
  • The hoistway has invisible blocking walls (Shaft Collision, on by default), open only at the landing entrances. They block pawns and physics bodies, so a character cannot walk into the shaft or fall into the pit.

Multiplayer settings are in the next section.

docs.title: Checklist for a custom character
docs.text:
1. Collision. The generated cabin parts block every channel except Camera, and the shaft walls block the Pawn and PhysicsBody channels. A standard Character capsule (Pawn object type) collides with both. If you changed your character's collision profile, make sure it still blocks WorldStatic and WorldDynamic.
  2. Movement mode. Use the standard Walking movement mode. In single player no special moving-base setup is needed on the character. For multiplayer, apply the settings below.
  3. Pressing buttons. Use the trace helper: on your interact input, call Trace Button from the camera (start at the camera location, direction along its forward vector, ignore yourself, distance 450 cm by default), then call Press Button on the result with the character's access level.
  4. Weight. A pawn in the cabin counts the car's Passenger Mass Kg (75 by default). Give the pawn a LFLoadComponent to count a different mass.
  5. Access level. Pass the access level of the player to Press Button, Select Floor, Call To Floor and the bank calls. The sample character uses level 0 and the operator panel level 9.

docs.title: Multiplayer settings
docs.text:
In multiplayer a custom character needs these settings to ride without jitter or fall-through. They come from the multiplayer tests (listen and dedicated server, 2 clients, 100 ms round trip, 1 % packet loss).

  1. bStayBasedInAir = true on the CharacterMovement component (Jumping / Falling). A jump inside a moving car then stays relative to the car. Client and server compare positions relative to the cabin floor, so corrections are rare, and a car moving up cannot pass through an airborne passenger. StayBasedInAirHeight can stay at its default (1000 cm, more than any cabin).
  2. Nothing else is needed for riding. CharacterMovement makes the car a tick prerequisite of the character automatically, and LiftForge makes the cabin floor and sills network-addressable. Do not move the car to a later tick group and do not drive it from a Timeline.
  3. Impart base velocity (bImpartBaseVelocityX/Y/Z): either setting is fine (the demo uses false). With bStayBasedInAir, no velocity is imparted while you jump inside the car.
  4. MaxStepHeight of 25 cm or more lets the character cross the landing sill smoothly.
  5. Crouch: set NavAgentProps.bCanCrouch on the movement component. Crouching while riding is smooth and replicates.
  6. Sprint: replicate it the usual way (a custom move flag). Changing MaxWalkSpeed on the server and the client independently causes corrections in any game.
  7. Network smoothing: the default (Exponential) is fine. Other players riding with you stay planted on the floor.
  8. A pawn without CharacterMovement (a VR pawn): add LFRiderComponent. It carries the pawn on each machine but does not replicate movement. For multiplayer VR, use a Character-based pawn.
  9. Interactor: each player needs a LFElevatorInteractorComponent. The server adds it automatically. Set its AccessLevel in your game mode's Post Login to unlock restricted floors.
  10. Save the map before multiplayer Play In Editor. See the Multiplayer guide.

docs.title: Enhanced Input
docs.text:
The sample pawns use Enhanced Input. You can reuse the assets or use your own.

Action Type Desktop VR IA_LF_Move Axis2D (X right, Y forward) W A S D W A S D and the left thumbstick or trackpad IA_LF_Look Axis2D (X yaw, Y pitch) Mouse not used IA_LF_Interact Boolean E and left mouse button E and the right trigger IA_LF_TogglePanel Boolean H not used IA_LF_ToggleVR Boolean V V IA_LF_Teleport Boolean not used T and the left trigger IA_LF_SnapTurn Axis1D (30 degrees past 0.7) not used Left and Right arrows and the right thumbstick or trackpad X

The assets are in /LiftForge/Input/ (IA_LF_*, IMC_LF_Desktop, IMC_LF_VR and the data asset DA_LF_DemoInput). To use your own, create a LFDemoInputConfig data asset, fill in your actions and mapping contexts, and select it in Project Settings > Plugins > LiftForge Demo > Input Config. An incomplete asset falls back to the defaults with a warning.

For your own character you only need your own Interact action: it calls Trace Button and Press Button. You do not have to use the LiftForge input assets at all.

docs.title: Spawn your own character in an example map
docs.text: In World Settings of LF_Showcase_Warm or LF_Showcase_Noir, set GameMode Override to your game mode and Default Pawn Class to your character. The map only uses the demo game mode through World Settings.

docs.title: Jitter and fall-through
docs.text: If the camera shakes in the car or the character sinks, see FAQ and troubleshooting.

docs.title: What LiftForge already does
docs.text:
• The geometry is built once per configuration. A hash saved with the actor skips the rebuild at construction and at BeginPlay when nothing changed.
  • Build assets are streamed in at BeginPlay and kept resident.
  • Repeated per-floor fixed parts (rail brackets, shaft lights, door tracks, frames, sills, display housings, hall stations) are instanced, one instanced component per mesh, material and collision group. This happens only when every material of the group has Used with Instanced Static Meshes enabled. All LiftForge master materials and material instances do. If you replace a material with your own, enable that flag on it, or those parts fall back to ordinary components.
  • Generated parts have no overlap events, so the roughly 100 parts of a moving cabin do not run overlap queries.
  • Displays and LED rings update only when their text or lit set changes.
  • Buttons tick only while their press animation plays.
  • A parked car (idle, doors closed, no calls, nothing to announce) ticks every Idle Tick Interval seconds (Project Settings > Plugins > LiftForge, default 0.1). Any call, door command, mode change or fault returns it to every frame. Set 0 to tick every frame.
  • The door light curtain is only read while the doors are not fully closed or while something is bound to On Obstruction Changed.
  • Decorative parts beyond Detail Draw Distance (8000 cm) are hidden. Collision on cabin floors, walls and doors stays on.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text: Tip How Large buildings Use instanced-friendly materials and keep Static Fixed Parts off unless the car never moves at runtime. Many cars Let cars park. Do not bind to events you do not use: the light curtain is queried more often when something is bound to the obstruction event. Draw distance Lower Detail Draw Distance on the preset for far-away shafts. Static lighting Static Fixed Parts gives cheaper fixed geometry but makes the actor's root Static and reports those parts as unbuilt until lighting is built. Exposure The example maps have a post process volume with manual exposure. Without one, a scene can render dark because of auto exposure. VR Turn on Apply VR Performance CVars (see VR setup). Measure on the headset runtime you target.

docs.title: Profiling
docs.text: Unreal Insights shows CPU trace scopes for ALFElevator::Tick, AnimateParts, UpdateDisplays, UpdateLoad, BuildAssembly and ALFElevatorBank::Tick. Use them to see which part of a car costs time.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text: Measured on the author's PC (RTX 5090, 2560 x 1440, UE 5.6 editor game session, software Lumen, nine cars moving, no NPCs): median frame time 2.9 to 3.6 ms, 95th percentile 4.9 to 6.3 ms across eight runs on the two maps. Your hardware will differ.

docs.title: The test of your own scene
docs.text: The plugin's -ElevatorBenchmark switch (development builds only) runs a scripted ride and writes a JSON report with frame and game-thread timings. The demo module's benchmark code is compiled out of shipping builds.

docs.title: Presets and visual sets
docs.text:
A preset (DA_Preset_<Key>) stores one elevator configuration so many cars can share it. A visual set (DA_VisualSet_<Key>) maps each part role (cabin wall, door frame, handrail and so on) to an authored mesh and its materials. A Blueprint (BP_LF_<Key>) is an elevator actor with the preset already assigned.

All three exist for these nine keys: Traction, MRL630, MRL1000, Goods2000, Bed2500, Panoramic, Hydraulic, Platform, Cycle.

Asset Path Presets /LiftForge/Presets/DA_Preset_<Key> Visual sets /LiftForge/VisualSets/DA_VisualSet_<Key> Blueprints /LiftForge/Blueprints/BP_LF_<Key> Example maps /LiftForge/Examples/Maps/LF_Showcase_Warm and /LiftForge/Examples/Maps/LF_Showcase_Noir

docs.title: Sizes
docs.text:
Passenger, goods, bed, panoramic and hydraulic cars stay within the EN 81-20 maximum car area for their rated load. Sizes are visualisation sizes, inspired by common ISO 4190-1 classes, and catalogue-neutral. The platform and cycle lift sizes are illustrative. Check the standard and your jurisdiction for real projects. Lengths are in centimetres. The sizes do not represent any manufacturer's product.

Preset Rated load Car W x D x H Door W x H Drive, doors Traction 800 kg, 10 persons 135 x 140 x 230 90 x 210 gearless traction, centre opening MRL630 630 kg, 8 persons 110 x 140 x 220 80 x 200 machine-room-less traction, side sliding MRL1000 1000 kg, 13 persons 160 x 140 x 230 90 x 210 machine-room-less traction, centre opening Goods2000 2000 kg 180 x 230 x 240 140 x 210 geared traction, telescopic Bed2500 2500 kg 200 x 240 x 240 130 x 210 gearless traction, telescopic Panoramic 1000 kg, 13 persons 150 x 150 x 250 90 x 210 gearless traction, centre opening, glazed walls Hydraulic 1000 kg 110 x 210 x 230 90 x 210 hydraulic, side sliding Platform 400 kg 110 x 140 x 210 90 x 190 hydraulic, hinged gate Cycle 500 kg 100 x 220 x 210 80 x 190 hydraulic, hinged gate
  • All presets use a 1.5 s door cycle.
  • The Platform speed is illustrative.
  • The MRL presets show a machine-room-less drive: the gearless machine sits on the rail tops and the controller is a cabinet beside the top landing door.

Every preset's cabin is authored at its exact size (walls, floor, ceiling, light, jambs, header, doors, handrails, sill, frame, toe guard and car operating panel cassette), each with its own design language: Traction walnut and bronze with a rear mirror; MRL630 oak and satin stainless; MRL1000 graphite laminate, brass trim and an LED cove; Goods2000 steel liner panels, bumper rails and a chequer floor; Bed2500 white HPL, vinyl floor, wide mirror and a fold-down seat; Panoramic faceted glass walls in a steel frame with a spotlight ring and a glazed hoistway; Hydraulic painted steel; Platform half-height powder-coated walls with a control column and a folding access ramp (lowered while the gate is open); Cycle rubber-lined walls with a wheel channel in the floor. The car operating panel sits on the right side wall next to the front on all nine presets (their return panels are narrower than 40 cm); a car with a return panel of 40 cm or more keeps it beside the door.

The demo building used by the example maps has the floors B2 (0 cm), B1 (320), G (680), M (950), L1 (1250), L2 (1620), L3 (1980) and L4 (2360). Each preset serves a subset of them.

docs.title: Use a preset
docs.text:
• Drag a BP_LF_<Key> into the level; or
  • add an LFElevator actor and set Preset to a DA_Preset_<Key>; or
  • pick it in the Elevator Builder.

To make a variant, either create your own preset asset (a LFElevatorPreset data asset) or turn on Use Configuration Override on one car.

Configuration fields: Shaft Material (a glass instance makes a glazed hoistway, as the panoramic preset uses), Cabin Screen (none, ceiling corner, side wall) with Cabin Screen Image, and Landing Wall Offset (how far the finished landing wall stands in front of the door plane; the hall station, lanterns and indicators are mounted on that face; 0 keeps the 1.0 layout). Mirror Capture gives the rear mirror panel a real reflection (a scene capture from the viewer's reflected position, one capture per frame while someone in front of it can see it: the doors are open, the viewer is inside the car, or the cabin is glazed); it needs the project setting Support global clip plane for Planar Reflections and is on in the Traction, MRL1000 and Bed2500 presets. Its edge smoothing relies on the main view's TSR or TAA (a sub-texel jitter on the capture that the temporal filter resolves); with FXAA, MSAA or no anti-aliasing the reflection is sharper but its edges are less smoothed. The mirror capture is untested in VR (see VR setup).

docs.title: Materials and finishes
docs.text:
Master materials are in /LiftForge/Materials/Masters: M_LF_Metal, M_LF_PowderCoat, M_LF_Wood, M_LF_Stone, M_LF_Fabric, M_LF_Glass, M_LF_Screen, M_LF_Poster, M_LF_Foliage, M_LF_Emissive, M_LF_Display, M_LF_Surface, M_LF_SkyDome and M_LF_MirrorCapture. Every finish is a material instance in /LiftForge/Materials/Instances (MI_LF_*). To change a finish, edit the instance:

Master Parameters Textured masters (metal, powder coat, wood, stone, fabric) BaseColor, Normal, ORM, Tiling (metres per repeat; 1 = 100 cm), UVRotation, Tint, TintStrength, RoughnessMin, RoughnessMax, NormalStrength, DetailNormal, DetailTiling, DetailStrength; metal adds Anisotropy, BrushAngle; fabric adds FuzzStrength M_LF_Surface Tint, Metallic, Roughness Emissive and display Color, EmissiveStrength M_LF_Glass Tint, Opacity, Roughness, IOR, FresnelExponent, SmudgeMask, SmudgeStrength M_LF_Screen ScreenImage, Brightness, PixelCount, GridStrength, FlipU, FlipV M_LF_Poster PosterImage, PaperRoughness, GlossStrength, FlipU, FlipV

Finish variants you can swap: woods Walnut, Oak, SmokedOak; stones Terrazzo, Travertine, TravertinePolished, Marble, StoneTile; metals Steel, Satin, Brass, Bronze, PanelSteel, LinerSteel, DarkMetal, Chequer; carpets Carpet, CarpetDark. Set a different instance in the visual set's Material Overrides for the slot you want to change.

The mesh material slots keep their authored names (M_HQ_Steel, M_HQ_Walnut and so on). A visual set maps each slot to an instance. All master materials have Used with Instanced Static Meshes enabled, so material instances can be used on the instanced parts of tall buildings.

docs.title: Meshes
docs.text:
• 291 part meshes (117 shared roles, 174 preset-specific parts) and 8 kit meshes. 30 of the shared meshes (for example SM_HQ_CabinDoor and SM_HQ_CabinFloor) are kit parts for your own visual sets: the presets and the example maps do not use them.
  • Each part mesh has 3 LODs: LOD0 authored in Blender, LOD1 (50 % of the triangles) and LOD2 (about 18 % on most meshes, up to 50 % on small parts) generated in Unreal. Each part has simple collision as authored (box; convex for the faceted and half-height walls; none for thin decorative parts, which then use their triangles) and a lightmap UV channel (coordinate index 1). Triangles over all unique part meshes: LOD0 728,333, LOD1 364,169, LOD2 131,695.
  • UVs are unwrapped at a real-world scale: 1 UV unit = 100 cm, so every CC0 surface material tiles at its physical size.
  • The 8 kit meshes are 1 m primitives with automatic collision and no LODs (188 or 764 triangles).
  • Decorative parts follow the configuration's Detail Draw Distance (8000 cm by default; 0 disables culling). Collision on the cabin floor, walls and doors stays available at any distance.
  • Nanite is not required.

docs.title: Signage
docs.text: LiftForge Signage actors (ALFSignage) show an image on any mesh whose image faces use the slots M_HQ_Screen (emissive LCD) or M_HQ_Poster (print). Choose a shipped mesh (ceiling-corner and wall cabin screens, lobby totem, landing screen, menu board, A1 and A2 poster frames, light box, directory board, wall sign) or keep your own mesh with Custom. Screen Image and Poster Image take any texture (35 samples ship: T_LF_Screen_<Name>, T_LF_Screen_<Name>_P portrait, T_LF_Poster_<Name>), Slides with Seconds Per Slide run a slideshow, and Media Texture shows a Media Framework texture (video) on the screen. Set Screen Image, Set Poster Image and Show Slide are Blueprint-callable. Nine of the sample images are not used by the example maps; they are extras for your own scenes.

docs.title: Textures and audio
docs.text:
• 62 surface maps in 22 sets (19 CC0 surface materials from ambientCG and Poly Haven, 3 procedural), base colour / DirectX normal / packed AO-roughness-metallic; walnut, oak, stone tile, terrazzo and steel at 4096 x 4096, the rest at 2048 x 2048. 35 signage images. Two HDRI cubemaps (T_LF_HDRI_PlacWolnosci and T_LF_HDRI_NeuerZollhof, Poly Haven, CC0), one per showcase look, for the sky light and sky dome.
  • 19 sound waves (9 effects, 10 spoken announcements) and 3 MetaSound sources (motor, pump, doors).
  • Replace any sound by assigning your own sound wave in the configuration's audio pack, or clear the slot. Announcements are optional: leave the floor's Announcement slot and the Doors Opening / Doors Closing slots empty for chime-only operation.
  • Configuration.Audio.Volume sets the overall volume of one car (0.35 in the presets).

docs.title: Lighting of the example maps
docs.text: All maps use dynamic Lumen lighting. There is nothing to bake.

docs.title: Known limits of the example maps
docs.text:
• Steel doors and panels in the cabins show cloudy reflections under software Lumen. Hardware Lumen removed them in our test, but took roughly two to three times the frame time.
  • The tower seen from the street is a plain block without windows, and a thin dark vertical band runs down its east wing.
  • The kerb joints in the forecourt read as a saw-tooth edge.
  • The Traction hero laylight shows one bright dot and two brighter patches.
  • The metal landing sills show dark blotches in close-up.

docs.title: Make your own visual set
docs.text: Create a ULFVisualSet data asset. Its Part Meshes map assigns a mesh to each role name (for example CabinWall or DoorFrame), with the mesh's authored size (Source Dimensions). The builder scales each part from that size to the size your configuration needs. The additive roles (MRLMachine, MRLController, HallLantern, LandingIndicator, CabinScreenCorner, CabinScreenWall, FoldSeat, Ramp, ControlColumn, GlassFrame, SpotRing, WheelChannel) are placed only when your set binds them. Set the Visual Set on a preset or a car. Leave it empty to build the car from the generated kit instead.

docs.title: Quick start (5 minutes)
docs.text: You will place a ready-made elevator in a new level and ride it.

docs.title: Option A: look at an example map first
docs.text:
1. Enable Show Plugin Content in the Content Browser.
  2. Open LiftForge Content/Examples/Maps/LF_Showcase_Warm or LF_Showcase_Noir.
  3. Press Play. The map sets the LiftForge demo game mode for you.
  4. Walk to a car with W A S D and the mouse, aim at a hall button and press E (or the left mouse button). Press H to open the operator panel.

docs.title: Option B: place an elevator in your own level
docs.text:
1. Open or create a level with a floor and enough room for a tall shaft. The elevator builds its own shaft, doors and landings.
  2. From LiftForge Content/Blueprints, drag BP_LF_Traction into the level. (Any BP_LF_<Key> works. See Presets and visual sets.)
  3. Select the actor. Under Elevator > Configuration you can see the Preset it uses. The floors, size, speed, doors and look all come from the preset.
  4. The actor origin is the reference for every floor: a floor's Elevation is its height above the actor origin, in centimetres. Move the actor so the lowest landing sits at the height of your floor.
  5. In World Settings, set GameMode Override to the LiftForge demo game mode (LFDemoGameMode). It spawns the sample desktop character. (If you use your own character, skip this step and read Using your own character.)
  6. Add a Player Start in front of the lowest landing and press Play.

docs.title: What you can do in play
docs.text:
Action Desktop Move W A S D Look Mouse Press the button you aim at E or left mouse button Operator panel (modes, faults, inspection) H Switch between desktop and VR pawn V

Press a hall button (up or down) to call the car. When the doors open, step in and press a floor button on the car operating panel. The car moves with a smooth acceleration and deceleration profile, levels at the landing, then opens the doors. They close again on their own after the dwell time.

The top passenger floor in the demo building is restricted. Cabin buttons use access level 0, and the operator panel uses level 9. See Access levels in Bank and destination dispatch.

docs.title: Control it from a Blueprint
docs.text:
Every way of operating a car goes through two functions on the elevator actor:

  • Execute Elevator Command: any command (a floor call, doors, a mode, a fault, an inspection toggle).
  • Call To Floor: a trip from a waiting floor to a destination.

Example: in a level Blueprint, get a reference to the elevator and call Move Elevator To Floor with a floor id such as L2. The node continues on Arrived when the car is level with the floor and the doors are fully open. See Blueprint API.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Change size, speed or floors: Elevator Builder.
  • Make several cars share calls: Bank and destination dispatch.
  • Drive your own character into the cabin: Using your own character.

• Questions on the Fab Q&A are usually answered within a few working days.
  • New Unreal Engine releases are supported soon after release.
  • Bugs are fixed in point releases (1.0.1, 1.0.2 and so on). See the Changelog.

Support covers the plugin and its documented behaviour. It does not cover custom gameplay code, other plugins or engine bugs, although I will say if I think the cause is one of them.

docs.title: A good bug report
docs.text:
Please include:

  1. LiftForge version and engine version (for example 1.0.0 on 5.7).
  2. What you expected and what happened.
  3. The Output Log around the problem (search it for LogLiftForge).
  4. The preset or configuration, and whether it is a bank or a single car.
  5. Whether it is single-player, a listen server or a dedicated server.
  6. A short project or level that reproduces it, if you can.

docs.title: Refunds
docs.text: Refunds are handled by Fab under its refund policy.

docs.title: VR setup (OpenXR)
docs.text: LiftForge ships a sample VR pawn (LFVRPawn) for OpenXR. It has not been tested on a real VR headset. Only simulated checks were run: the pawn riding a car, its input assets and its settings. Treat it as a starting point. VR is optional: desktop use needs no headset and no OpenXR plugin.

docs.title: Enable OpenXR
docs.text:
1. In Edit > Plugins, enable OpenXR (and the plugin for your headset runtime, if the runtime needs one), then restart the editor.
  2. Make sure a working OpenXR runtime is the active runtime on your PC (for example the one of your headset's software).
  3. Press Play > VR Preview, or use the V key in the demo to switch between the desktop character and the VR pawn.

LiftForge itself depends on the XRBase plugin only. The OpenXR plugin is a project decision.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Action Control Move Left thumbstick or trackpad (W A S D on the keyboard) Snap turn (30 degrees) Right thumbstick or trackpad X (Left and Right arrows) Press a button Right trigger (E on the keyboard), or touch the button with a controller Teleport Left trigger (T on the keyboard) Switch to desktop pawn V

The OpenXR controller profile keys for Touch, Index, Vive and Windows Mixed Reality are mapped. You can remap everything; see Using your own character.

docs.title: Riding in VR
docs.text: LFVRPawn carries a LFRiderComponent. For your own VR pawn add a LFRiderComponent too, use a collidable root, and keep the camera and controllers below a tracking-origin component (the sample pawn calls it VROrigin). The rider component moves the pawn root with the cabin floor and leaves the local head and hand tracking alone.

docs.title: VR performance
docs.text:
In Project Settings > Plugins > LiftForge Demo turn on Apply VR Performance CVars (off by default). While the sample VR pawn runs on a headset it then turns off dynamic global illumination and reflections (r.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod 0, r.ReflectionMethod 0), and restores your previous values when the pawn ends play. Frame timing on a real headset must be measured on the OpenXR runtime you target.

The Laser Material setting in the same panel is the material of the VR pointer beam.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The desktop operator panel (key H) is a desktop feature. In VR use the physical consoles.
  • If the pawn falls through the car, check that it has a collidable root and a LFRiderComponent (see FAQ).
  • Cabin mirrors are untested in VR. The mirror capture (LFMirrorCaptureComponent) renders one view from the camera's reflected position and has no per-eye handling, and it has not been run on a headset. On a VR project treat it as unsupported: switch off Mirror Capture on the preset to get the plain mirror finish.

docs.title: World Partition notes
docs.text: LiftForge is designed for World Partition levels, but has not been tested in one. A few rules keep banks working when cars and banks are in different cells.

docs.title: Link cars and bank by name, not by reference
docs.text:
A hard actor reference from a bank to a car (or from a car to a bank) forces both actors to load together. Instead give the car and the bank the same Bank Name:

  1. Set Bank Name on the bank actor, for example North.
  2. Set the same Bank Name on each car.

Cars and banks register with the world's LiftForge registry (LFElevatorRegistry, a world subsystem) when they begin play and unregister when they end play. With World Partition they therefore appear and disappear as their cells stream in, and find each other without hard references.

  • Calls are assigned to the cars that are loaded. A call assigned to a car that unloads is re-assigned on the next bank tick (every 0.1 s).
  • A bank with no loaded cars logs one warning and rejects calls (No Elevator Available).
  • Query the registry in Blueprints with Get Elevators, Get Bank Members, Find Bank and Get Banks on the LFElevatorRegistry subsystem.

docs.title: One car is one actor
docs.text: A car and its shaft, landings and doors are generated by a single actor. It loads and unloads as a whole. Treat it like any other large actor: decide in your project whether it should be spatially loaded, or placed in an always-loaded data layer if players must be able to call it from far away.

docs.title: Streaming of the car's own assets
docs.text: At BeginPlay a car loads the kit, the visual set and the materials it needs and keeps them resident, so the first build does not stall the game thread. Everything is referenced softly.

docs.title: Large buildings
docs.text: Hall stations, rail brackets, shaft lights, door tracks and frames repeat on every floor. When all of their materials have Used with Instanced Static Meshes enabled (all LiftForge masters and instances do), they are drawn as instanced meshes. See Performance tips.
